## PR1 trail facts

| Distance | 6.1 km, Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo

| Down to Achada do Teixeira | about 2.8 km by PR1.2

| Time | about 3 hours to Pico Ruivo; about 4 hours in all

| Difficulty | Moderate

| Altitude | 1,491–1,857 m

| Direction | One-way beyond Pedra Rija (Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija, 1.2 km, both ways)

| Fee | €10.50 full route · €4.50 Areeiro–Pedra Rija only

| Tunnels | Yes, bring a headlamp

Distance, time, difficulty and altitude: Visit Madeira PR1 page. Direction: IFCN. Fees: SIMplifica and Portaria 48/2026.

## Is PR1 one-way? Yes, beyond Pedra Rija

- Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo (full route): one-way only. In force since the full reopening on 1 May 2026 (Fridays to Sundays at first, every day since 26 June 2026). You can't walk it from Pico Ruivo back to Pico do Areeiro.

- Pico do Areeiro ↔ Miradouro da Pedra Rija (1.2 km each way): two-way. A there-and-back from the Areeiro car park.

- Two different SIMplifica tickets: €4.50 for Areeiro–Pedra Rija only, €10.50 for the full route (the PR1.1, PR1.2 and PR1.3 exits are included). Booked through an IFCN protocol operator: €3 / €7. Ages 12 and under go free but must be on the booking.

- You finish at Achada do Teixeira, down PR1.2 from Pico Ruivo (about an hour). No bus goes there, so plan the ride back first: getting back without a car · sunrise transport to Pico do Areeiro.

Official sources disagree right now. IFCN's warnings list (its "updated" date is on the status card above) still lists the one-way Pedra Rija → Pico Ruivo section as closed after the September walkway works, while Visit Madeira shows PR1 open. Before you go, check whether SIMplifica sells full-route (€10.50) slots for your date.

## Recent closures and reopenings

- 14 Aug 2024: a wildfire in the central mountains; PR1 closes after a major rockfall beyond Pedra Rija.

- 4 Sep 2024: Pico do Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija reopens, two-way. The rest stays closed.

- 1 May 2026: the full route reopens, one-way beyond Pedra Rija, Fridays to Sundays only.

- 26 Jun 2026: the one-way section opens every day.

- 14–17 and 21–22 Sep 2026: Pedra Rija → Pico Ruivo closed for scheduled works; Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija stays open both ways.

- Coming up, Sun 4 Oct 2026, 07:55–10:20: Eco Rally Madeira road closures on the Eira do Serrado road, the Serras de Santo António forest road (to the ER202) and the Chão da Lagoa road (Funchal council Edital 738/2026). Allow extra time driving up, or use the Poiso road.

Sources: IFCN warnings list · Visit Madeira, PR1 · Portaria 48/2026 (fees) · Edital 738/2026 · DN, 28 Oct 2024

## Sold out? What can I do if PR1 slots are gone on SIMplifica?

PR1 has capacity limits and 30-minute entry slots. Morning windows go first. In order of what actually works:

- Try weekday, mid-morning slots. Everyone fights for sunrise. 09:00–10:30 midweek is often available days after dawn slots are gone — and you skip the parking chaos.

- Re-check the SIMplifica booking page the evening before. Cancellations get released back. Rescheduled bookings free up slots with no notice.

- Book through an IFCN protocol operator. Licensed guides hold their own allocation and handle the permit for you (their trail fee is discounted to €7 on PR1). Costs more overall, solves transport too.

- Do the summit anyway — from the other side. PR1.2 from Achada do Teixeira reaches Pico Ruivo (1,862 m, the island's highest point) in about 45–60 min each way. Standard €4.50 fee, its own booking, usually far more availability.

PR1 is paid via SIMplifica and not included in the 1/3/7-day multi-day passes. The fee depends on which section is open: €4.50 for the Pico do Areeiro–Pedra Rija section, or €10.50 for the full one-way traverse to Pico Ruivo when open. Ages 12 and under free; parking €4.00/hour. Check the live status above for today.

## Sunrise? How to do PR1 at dawn

Sunrise above the clouds at Pico do Areeiro is why so many people on Madeira set a 4 a.m. alarm. The rules confuse everyone, so here's the short version:

- Do I need a ticket to watch the sunrise at Pico do Areeiro? Most likely not, but check. The fee applies to entering the classified trail, and the viewpoint is by the car park, outside it. We found no explicit official statement, so if in doubt ask IFCN or check SIMplifica. Walking onto PR1 itself always needs a ticket for your slot.

- Hiking at first light needs the earliest slot: 07:00–07:30. Early 07:00 and 07:30 slots were added in June 2026 because of sunrise demand — before that, entry started at 08:00. Same fee as any other window; there is no sunrise surcharge.

- Match the slot to the season. Sunrise ranges from about 06:50 in midsummer to 08:05 in midwinter. In summer, watch it from the viewpoint, then start walking at 07:00. In late autumn and winter, the 07:00 slot puts you on the ridge in the dark for sunrise from the trail itself — bring a headlamp.

- Parking is the real bottleneck. Arrive at least an hour before sunrise: the lots fill, cars line the access road, and police sometimes close it when it saturates. And dress warm — it can be single digits °C at 1,818 m before dawn even in August.

The no-car version: sunrise transfer minibuses pick up in Funchal/Caniço around 05:00–05:30, drop you at the summit before dawn and collect you at Achada do Teixeira after the traverse — solving parking and the one-way return in one go. The trail ticket usually isn't included: book it yourself, or go with an IFCN protocol operator (€7).

The 07:00–07:30 window is the first to sell out — often days ahead in July–August. Book as far ahead as SIMplifica allows and re-check the evening before for released cancellations.

## Closed? How do I reschedule my SIMplifica booking?

If IFCN officially closes the trail (weather, rockfall, works), you're entitled to change — but there's a procedure:

- Contact the SIMplifica call centre before your scheduled date. Not IFCN — they don't manage the portal.

- You can move to a different date or time on the same trail freely.

- You can switch to a different trail only if yours was officially closed by the authorities. A change of plans on your side doesn't qualify.

Open alternatives that don't feel like a consolation prize:

- PR1.2 Vereda do Pico Ruivo — the summit without the ridge. Moderate, family-doable.

- PR9 Levada do Caldeirão Verde — tunnels, waterfalls, green canyon. Bring a headlamp.

- PR11 Vereda dos Balcões — 3 km, nearly flat, big valley views. The easy win on a foggy summit day.

## Three things people find out too late

- PR1 is one-way now (since the 1 May 2026 reopening): beyond Pedra Rija, Areeiro → Ruivo only. You finish at Achada do Teixeira — plan your ride back before you start.

- No cash, no kiosk for PR1. Booking is online-only. Walking an IFCN classified trail without a valid SIMplifica ticket is an administrative offence (Portaria 801/2025 art. 10; DLR 24/2022/M art. 13); the law sets fines for individuals of €250–€2,500.

- Summit weather ≠ Funchal weather. It can be 10–15°C colder at 1,800 m, with fog while the coast is sunny. Check the mountain forecast, not the city one.

PR1.2.text:
## Is Pico Ruivo open today?

Vereda do Pico Ruivo (PR1.2) — Achada do Teixeira to Madeira's highest point (1,862 m), the gentlest way up. Status from the official IFCN warnings list, with IFCN's own “updated” date. See all Madeira trails or PR1.

## PR1.2 trail facts

| Distance | 2.8 km each way

| Round trip | 5.6 km

| Time | ~1h30 each way

| Difficulty | Moderate

| Summit | 1,862 m

| Type | Out-and-back

| Fee | €4.50

## PR1.2 trailhead

Open in OpenStreetMap · Google Maps

Trailhead location: Visit Madeira.

## Book it. PR1.2 on SIMplifica

This is the short route to the summit, and a sunrise favourite, so slots go fast.

- Book your €4.50 slot on SIMplifica in advance, in a 30-minute window. Under-12s are free but must be on the booking.

- Sunrise slots go first. If you want the summit at dawn, book early and expect company; mid-morning is quieter.

- Coming off PR1? If you cross from Pico do Areeiro on PR1, you finish above here — see getting back from PR1.

PR1.2 is €4.50 per person, paid on SIMplifica; under-12s and residents free but counted on the reservation. Check the live status above before you drive up.

## Getting there. Achada do Teixeira

The walk starts at the Achada do Teixeira car park, high above Santana on the north side — about an hour's drive from Funchal.

- Drive to the Achada do Teixeira car park (this is also where PR1 finishes). There's a shelter and a viewpoint; parking is limited at sunrise.

- From the car park, a built stone path climbs steadily to the Pico Ruivo mountain shelter (Casa de Abrigo), then a short final push to the 1,862 m summit — Madeira's highest point.

- It's the easiest way to the top: no exposed ridge, just a steady paved climb of roughly 200 m of ascent.

## What's the weather at Vereda do Pico Ruivo (PR1.2) now?

The status card above shows the latest measured reading from the IPMA Pico do Areeiro station, the regional weather station nearest the trail: temperature, wind and whether it is likely in cloud. Expect the mountains cooler and cloudier than Funchal.

Official weather warnings for the Madeira mountains: IPMA.

## Closed or full? Your options

If IFCN closes PR1.2 (weather, works) or you can't get a slot:

- Reschedule via the SIMplifica call centre before your date — date/time freely, another trail only if yours was officially closed.

- Open alternatives: check the live board — Caldeirão Verde (PR9) and Balcões (PR11) are usually available.

## Three things people find out too late

- Summit weather ≠ Funchal weather. At 1,862 m it can be cold, windy and in cloud while the coast is sunny — you may be above a sea of clouds, or in one. Bring a warm layer and check the live status.

- It's a climb, not a stroll. The stone path gains height steadily to the shelter; easy underfoot but a proper uphill, especially at altitude.

- Nothing's open up there. The shelter is basic — no shop or reliable signal. Carry water, snacks and a headtorch for a dark start.

## Questions people ask

## Is Pico Ruivo open today?

Today's status is shown live at the top of this page, taken from the official IFCN warnings list, which carries IFCN's own “updated” date. Access is €4.50 through the SIMplifica portal; children under 12 are free but must be on the booking.

## What is the easiest way to Pico Ruivo?

The Vereda do Pico Ruivo (PR1.2) from Achada do Teixeira — about 2.8 km each way on a built stone path — is the shortest and gentlest route to the summit, far easier than the long PR1 ridge from Pico do Areeiro.

## Do you need to book Pico Ruivo?

Yes. PR1.2 requires an advance booking and €4.50 payment through SIMplifica, in a 30-minute entry slot. It is popular for sunrise, so book ahead in summer.

## How long is the walk to Pico Ruivo from Achada do Teixeira?

About 2.8 km each way (5.6 km round trip), roughly 1 hour 30 minutes each way, graded moderate. It is a steady stone-paved climb to the shelter and the 1,862 m summit, then back the same way.

PR6.text:
## 25 Fontes (PR6): open today? Booking, one-way loop & shuttle 2026

Levada das 25 Fontes (PR6), from Rabaçal to the lagoon of the 25 springs. The status below comes from the official IFCN warnings list and carries IFCN's own "updated" date. See all Madeira trails or PR1.

Trail status comes from the official IFCN warnings list, which IFCN updates when conditions change and dates itself ("updated"). It is shown here as a live badge (it needs JavaScript). If it doesn't appear, check the official sources linked below.

## PR6 trail facts

| Distance | 4.3 km each way

| Time | ~3 hours

| Difficulty | Moderate

| Altitude | 964–1,288 m

| Start | Rabaçal (ER105)

| Return | By the Bypass

| Fee | €4.50

| Exposure | High (vertigo)

| Tunnels | None

| Torch | Not needed

## PR6 trailhead

Open in OpenStreetMap · Google Maps

Trailhead location: Visit Madeira.

## Book it. How to book PR6 in 2026

- Book a slot on SIMplifica: €4.50 per person over 12. Children 12 and under are free but must be on the booking; so must Madeira residents. It is online only; nothing is sold at Rabaçal.

- Pick a 30-minute entry window. IFCN allows about 15 minutes' tolerance either side. It's an allowance, not a right. Same-day booking works if slots remain; hiking guides report that morning slots in July and August go days ahead.

- Adding Risco (PR6.1) or another Rabaçal trail? Each one is a separate SIMplifica item with its own slot. Put them all in one booking: two or more trails in a day are charged the €9 day rate automatically (€22.50 over 3 days, €52.50 over 7).

- Through a tour operator with an IFCN protocol the trail fee is €3.

Walking PR6 without a valid ticket is an administrative offence; the law sets fines for individuals of €250–€2,500. The fee is refunded, or moved to a new date within a year, only if IFCN closes the trail on your date: email helpdesk.ifcn@madeira.gov.pt within 10 working days. Rain or a change of plans doesn't count. All 2026 fees and a cost calculator · Step-by-step SIMplifica booking

## One way at the end. Out by the levada, back by the Bypass

Since the works on the Bypass were finished, IFCN runs PR6 with controlled one-way circulation: you walk out from Rabaçal to 25 Fontes along the Levada das 25 Fontes and come back by the alternative section called the Bypass.

The IFCN trailhead panel puts the one-way section between km 3.3 and km 4.1. Follow the signs; everywhere else you walk the same path back.

Visit Madeira's PR6 page still says the one-way section "will operate in both directions". That note dates from the Bypass works. IFCN's list (updated 14 September 2026) gives the current rule.

IFCN's panel warns: "PR 6 can cause vertigo. Do not put weight on protection barriers." The levada path is narrow in places with drops beside it.

## Getting there. Parking and the Rabaçal shuttle

- Park at the car park on the ER105 above Rabaçal. It is free, according to 2026 reports. The trail fee does not include parking.

- Shuttle: the Calheta council runs a vehicle between the ER105 car park and the Casa Florestal do Rabaçal trailhead, daily 10:00–18:00, €5 one way or €8 return (CM Calheta; driver +351 966 426 851). The payment method isn't stated officially; guides report cash only, so bring some.

- Or walk the 2 km tarmac road down to the trailhead. It's easy going down, but you climb it back up at the end, when you're tired.

- Taxi: the IFCN panel lists Táxis Calheta, +351 291 822 129.

There's no fuel or shop up at Rabaçal. Bring water, layers and anything you need before you leave the coast.

## PR6 by bus

No public bus reaches Rabaçal: none of the bus lines on SIGA serves the Paul da Serra plateau or the Fanal. You need a car, a taxi or a tour transfer. From the Rabaçal car park on the ER110, the Calheta council runs a shuttle down to the Rabaçal house (pay in cash).

## Make a day of it: Risco and the tunnel

- Levada do Risco (PR6.1) starts at the same place and ends at a tall waterfall. Visit Madeira calls it easy and suitable for the whole family. It is its own booking. Two trails on the same day cost €9, and a third Rabaçal trail that day adds nothing: the €9 day rate covers two or more.

- Vereda da Lagoa do Vento (PR6.3) is another Rabaçal trail with its own booking.

- Túnel do Cavalo (PR6.6) is a separate classified trail (2.3 km) from the Caldeira leisure area up to Casa do Rabaçal, through the ~800 m Túnel do Cavalo. IFCN's panel says to carry a torch. If you come up this way, book PR6.6 as well as PR6. The standard PR6 route has no tunnel.

## What's the weather at Levada das 25 Fontes (PR6) now?

The status card above shows the latest measured reading from the IPMA Rabaçal station, the regional weather station nearest the trail: temperature, wind and whether it is likely in cloud. Expect the mountains cooler and cloudier than Funchal.

Official weather warnings for the Madeira mountains: IPMA.

## Closed or full? Your options

- If IFCN closes PR6 on your date, email helpdesk.ifcn@madeira.gov.pt within 10 working days with your tickets and invoice, and ask for a new date within a year or a refund. The SIMplifica contact centre can't change bookings.

- If you can't get a slot, check the live board for open alternatives such as Risco (PR6.1), Caldeirão Verde (PR9) or Balcões (PR11).

## Three things people find out too late

- The return is uphill. Unless you take the shuttle, the 2 km road you walked down at the start is a real climb at the end.

- It's laurel forest at 964–1,288 m. It can be cool, damp or foggy while Funchal is sunny. Bring a layer and grippy shoes.

- The drops are real. IFCN rates it a vertigo risk. Keep children close and don't lean on the barriers.

## Questions people ask

## Do I need to book the 25 Fontes (PR6)?

Yes. PR6 needs a SIMplifica booking for a 30-minute entry slot, €4.50 per person over 12 (€3 through a tour operator with an IFCN protocol). Children 12 and under are free but must be on the booking.

## Is the 25 Fontes open today?

The live card at the top of this page shows the official status from the IFCN warnings list, with IFCN's own "updated" date. Check it before you pay: the fee is refunded only when IFCN closes the trail.

## Is the 25 Fontes trail one-way?

At the end, yes. IFCN runs controlled one-way circulation: out to 25 Fontes along the levada, back by the section called the Bypass (between km 3.3 and 4.1). Follow the signs.

## How much is the Rabaçal shuttle to the 25 Fontes?

The Calheta council shuttle between the ER105 car park and the Rabaçal trailhead costs €5 one way or €8 return and runs daily from 10:00 to 18:00. Otherwise you walk the 2 km road.

## Is parking free at Rabaçal?

Yes, the car park on the ER105 above Rabaçal is free, according to 2026 reports. Parking is not part of the trail fee.

## Do I need a torch for the 25 Fontes?

Not on the standard PR6 route, which has no tunnel. You do need one on the Túnel do Cavalo (PR6.6) access from Calheta, which is a separate trail with its own booking.

## Watch the wind. Why it closes

São Lourenço is the one trail where the live status matters most. The peninsula is fully exposed with no shelter, so IFCN closes it when the north wind is strong — it can be open one day and shut the next.

- Check the status above the morning you go, not the night before. A booked slot is no use if it's closed for wind.

- No shade, no water, full sun — this is a semi-arid coast, not a green levada. Bring sun protection, a windproof layer and plenty of water.

Unlike the inland levadas, the danger here is sun, heat and wind — not cold. On a fierce-wind or scorching day, save it and pick a shaded trail instead.

## Book it. PR8 on SIMplifica

- Book your €4.50 slot on SIMplifica in advance, in a 30-minute window. Under-12s free but on the booking.

The walk starts at Baía d'Abra, at the very eastern end of the island — about 45 minutes' drive from Funchal along the ER214.

- Park at the Baía d'Abra car park at the road's end; it fills up in high season.

- The path undulates along the peninsula — reddish, ochre volcanic rock and big sea views on both sides — out to Casa do Sardinha, with two islets beyond the tip.

- Look for seabirds and, if you're lucky, monk seals in the bays below.

## Book it. PR9 on SIMplifica

A long, green classic through tunnels to a 100-metre waterfall — and a busy one.

- Book your €4.50 slot on SIMplifica in advance, in a 30-minute window. Under-12s free but on the booking.

- Start early. It's a 5–6 hour day; an early slot gives you daylight, cooler tunnels and thinner crowds.

PR9 is €4.50 per person on SIMplifica, plus ~€2.00/hour parking at Queimadas. Under-12s and residents free but counted. Check the live status above before you drive north.

## Getting there. Queimadas (Santana)

The walk starts at the Queimadas Forest Park, above Santana on the green north coast — about an hour from Funchal.

- Drive to the Queimadas car park and its pretty thatched houses; parking is paid (~€2.00/hour). The levada path begins here.

- It's a long, mostly level walk along an 18th-century levada through Laurissilva forest to the Caldeirão Verde — a green pool under a ~100 m cascade.

- Keen walkers continue on the full PR9 to Caldeirão do Inferno (about 8.7 km each way) — much longer; most turn around at the Caldeirão Verde waterfall.

## PR9 by bus

Getting there. No bus goes up to Queimadas. Take a CAM bus to Santana, then a taxi up to the Queimadas forest park (ask the fare when you book). CAM's Santana-line buses, Funchal → Santana. Monday to Friday: 07:30 → 09:00, 08:10 → 10:00, 09:00 → 10:25, 10:00 → 11:25. Saturdays: 07:30 → 09:13, 10:00 → 11:20. Sundays and holidays: 07:30 → 09:18, 10:30 → 12:00.

## Bring a torch. The tunnels & the drops

- Four tunnels are carved into the rock — some long, dark and dripping. A headtorch (or phone torch) is essential; it's genuinely dark inside.

- The levada edge is narrow with big drops in places, often with a handrail — not one for a strong fear of heights.

- Wear grippy shoes and expect wet feet; the north side is damp and the tunnels drip.

- It's a full day. 5–6 hours and ~13 km there and back — start early and carry water and food.

- The tunnels are dark and wet. No torch means feeling your way in the dark; bring one and grippy shoes.

- North and damp. It can be foggy, wet and cooler than the coast, and the ledges are narrow — go steady and mind the drops.

## PR10 trailhead

Open in OpenStreetMap · Google Maps

Trailhead location: Visit Madeira.

## Open today? Why this one matters

The Levada do Furado is one of the island's oldest and most loved levada walks — and also one of the most frequently closed. It runs along steep, wooded ravines that shed rock and mud after heavy rain, so IFCN shuts sections of it more often than the easier trails.

That's exactly why the live badge above matters: don't book, drive out, or plan your day around PR10 until it shows OPEN today. If it's closed, the alternatives below start from the same valley.

## Book it. PR10 on SIMplifica

Once the trail shows open, booking is the same as any paid PR trail:

- Book your €4.50 slot on SIMplifica. Under-12s and residents are free but must still be named on the booking. Book only after you've confirmed today's status — this trail closes often, and a closure is the one case where you can switch trail.

- Or go with an IFCN protocol operator — a lower trail fee (€3) plus transport, which also solves the return from Portela (see below).

PR10 is paid via SIMplifica on its own separate booking and not included in the multi-day passes. €4.50 per person; under-12s and residents free but counted on the reservation. Check the live status above before you pay.

## The catch. It ends at Portela, not your car

The Furado is linear: you start at Ribeiro Frio (on the ER103, ~860 m) and finish about 11 km later at Portela — a different place entirely. Sorting the return before you set off is the single thing people get wrong.

- Two cars or a taxi. Leave one car at Portela, or pre-book a taxi to collect you there — phone signal at Portela is patchy, so arrange it in advance.

- A guided walk with transfers is the easiest fix: you're dropped at Ribeiro Frio and picked up at Portela, no car shuffle.

- Buses are infrequent. Don't count on turning up at Portela and catching one — check times the day before, or you'll be stuck.

Same one-way headache as PR1 — see getting back without a car for the general playbook on Madeira's point-to-point trails.

## PR10 by bus (CAM): getting there is easy, getting back isn't

Getting there. Ribeiro Frio, the start, is a stop on CAM's Santana-line buses from Funchal. The walk is about 11 km, so take a morning bus. Monday to Friday: 08:10 (route 801, at Ribeiro Frio about 08:50), 09:00 (801, 09:41) and 10:00 (801, 10:41). Saturdays: 07:30 (850, 08:12) and 10:00 (801, 10:42). Sundays and holidays: 07:30 (850, 08:12) and 10:30 (801, 11:15).

Getting back. Portela, where the walk ends, is on CAM lines 53 and 78 (new no. 825) back towards Machico and Funchal, but their timetables print no time at Portela. Ask CAM for the time it passes before you set off, or pre-book a taxi to collect you there.

Times as printed on CAM's Santana network timetable; times at intermediate stops are approximate and can change with traffic or bad weather. No buses on 25 December. Check before you travel with CAM: info@cam-madeira.pt, +351 291 201 150.

## If it's closed — same valley, still walking

Ribeiro Frio is a trailhead hub, so a closed Furado doesn't waste the drive:

- Vereda dos Balcões (PR11) — starts from the very same Ribeiro Frio, an easy 1.5 km each way to a famous laurel-forest viewpoint. Usually open. See Balcões →

- Ribeiro Frio itself — a trout hatchery, cafés and shade under the laurisilva, worth a stop either way.

- Greener day trips: Caldeirão Verde (PR9) and 25 Fontes (PR6) are usually available and just as lush.

If IFCN closes PR10 (the usual reasons: storm damage, landslip, works) or you can't get a slot:

- Reschedule via the SIMplifica call centre before your date — you can move date/time freely, and switch to another trail only if yours was officially closed.

- Open alternatives: check the live board — Balcões (PR11), Caldeirão Verde (PR9) and Fanal (PR13) are usually available.

## Three things people find out too late

- It closes more than most. Plan a backup for the same day so a last-minute closure doesn't sink the whole trip — Balcões from the same car park is the obvious one.

- It needs a head for heights. Parts of the levada path are narrow with a sheer drop and no rail, and there are a couple of low rock passages — bring a torch and sure-footed shoes, and skip it in bad weather.

- You don't finish where you started. Portela is 11 km from Ribeiro Frio — fix the return first, or you'll be hitching in the dark.

The Levada do Furado is a linear (point-to-point) walk that finishes at Portela, not where you started at Ribeiro Frio. Most people use two cars, a pre-booked taxi, or a guided tour with transfers. Public buses from Portela are infrequent, so plan the return before you set off.

About 11 km one way from Ribeiro Frio to Portela, roughly 4 hours, graded moderate. There are narrow, exposed sections with drops and a couple of low rock passages, so it needs a head for heights and sure footing.

## The forest. Those misty trees

Fanal is the picture everyone comes for: ancient, gnarled til (laurel) trees in the mist, high on the Paúl da Serra plateau — part of the UNESCO Laurissilva.

- The fog is the magic. The scene works best when cloud rolls through the trees; a clear blue day is pretty but far less atmospheric.

- Two things share the name. The classified Vereda do Fanal (PR13) is a 10.8 km walk across the plateau; the Fanal forest at the end (with the famous trees and picnic meadow) is also reachable by car on the ER209.

## Book it. PR13 on SIMplifica

- Book the PR13 trail's €4.50 slot on SIMplifica in advance, in a 30-minute window. Under-12s free but on the booking.

- Just visiting the forest by car? The classified walk is what's booked; whether a slot is also needed simply to wander the Fanal forest area is worth confirming on SIMplifica, as access rules are tightening.

Check the live status above before the long drive up — the plateau closes for weather, and it's a remote spot to find a closed gate.

## Getting there. The Paúl da Serra plateau

Fanal is remote: a high, exposed plateau in the west, over an hour from Funchal via the ER110 and ER209.

- It's high and often in cloud (1,130–1,420 m) — that's the point, but it means cold, damp and low visibility. Bring warm, waterproof layers even in summer.

- Fuel up and go prepared: no shops, patchy signal, and mist that can drop visibility fast. Don't rely on a phone map alone.

- The full PR13 is 10.8 km, ~4 hours across the plateau to the forest and its volcanic crater — a proper walk, not just the photo stop.

## PR13 by bus

No public bus reaches Fanal: none of the bus lines on SIGA serves the Paul da Serra plateau or the Fanal. You need a car, a taxi or a tour transfer.

- It's high and cold. The plateau can be foggy and near-freezing while Funchal is in shorts — go dressed for the mountains.

- The trail ≠ the photo stop. The full PR13 is a 10.8 km / 4-hour walk; the famous trees are at the Fanal end, which you can also drive to.

- Remote and exposed. No facilities, patchy signal, and fast-changing mist — carry water, food, layers and don't rely on your phone alone.

Fanal sits high on the exposed Paúl da Serra plateau (~1,150–1,420 m), where moist Atlantic air condenses over the laurel forest. The mist among the ancient, gnarled til trees is exactly what makes the photos — but it also means cold, damp and low visibility, so dress warm.

The Levada do Rei is one of Madeira's classic laurel-forest walks — quieter than the 25 Fontes, but still popular. In order of what matters:

- Book your €4.50 slot on SIMplifica in advance. Under-12s and residents are free but must still be on the booking. Check the live status above before you pay.

PR18 is paid via SIMplifica on its own separate booking and not included in the multi-day passes. €4.50 per person; under-12s and residents free but counted on the reservation.

## Getting there. São Jorge & the ETAR trailhead

The trail starts above São Jorge, on the island's green north coast — about an hour's drive from Funchal over the mountains.

- Park at the ETAR (the small water-treatment station) at the end of the access road above São Jorge, where the levada path begins. There's only a small parking area and no shuttle, so come early or car-share.

- It's out-and-back, so unlike the point-to-point trails you finish back at your car — no return transport to arrange.

- The road up is narrow. Take it slowly, especially in the damp; the north coast catches more cloud and rain than the south.

There's no shop or café at the trailhead. Bring water, a layer and a rain shell — the north side is greener because it's wetter, and the forest can be cool and dripping even when the coast is bright.

## What it's like

This is a walk for the forest, not the views. The levada runs almost level through some of the best-preserved laurisilva — the UNESCO World Heritage laurel forest — heavy with moss, ferns and birdsong, ending at the Ribeiro Bonito, the pretty stream-source where the channel's water begins.

- Green and shaded the whole way, with a few little waterfalls crossing the path.

- Much quieter than Rabaçal or Caldeirão Verde — if you want a calm levada day, this is the one.

- Level and family-friendly, though the levada edge is narrow in places and the ground can be muddy and slick after rain.

fees.text:
## Madeira hiking fees 2026

What each official PR trail costs in 2026, who pays nothing, the 1-, 3- and 7-day combined rates, refunds and fines, plus a calculator for your trip. Set by Portaria 801/2025, as amended by Portaria 48/2026.

The short answer: €4.50 per person per trail. PR1 is €4.50 to Pedra Rija and back, or €10.50 for the full route to Pico Ruivo. Two or more trails in one day cost €9, in 3 days €22.50, in 7 days €52.50 (PR1 never counts). Children 12 and under, Madeira residents and people with a 60%+ disability pay nothing but must still book. You pay online on SIMplifica only.

## 2026 fee table

Per person. Amounts for non-residents, in force since 1 January 2026 (Portaria 48/2026, Annex I).

| Ticket | On your own | Via an operator with an IFCN protocol

| Any classified PR trail (except PR1) | €4.50 | €3.00

| PR1 Areeiro → Miradouro da Pedra Rija and back (no access to Pico Ruivo) | €4.50 | €3.00

| PR1 full route Areeiro → Pico Ruivo (includes the PR1.1, PR1.2 and PR1.3 exits) | €10.50 | €7.00

| Day rate: 2 or more trails in one day (excl. PR1) | €9.00 | €6.00

| 3-day rate: 2 or more trails in 3 days (excl. PR1) | €22.50 | €15.00

| 7-day rate: 2 or more trails in 7 days (excl. PR1) | €52.50 | €35.00

- The day and multi-day rates aren't passes. Every trail still needs its own booking and time slot. SIMplifica has no button for them: put all your trails in one booking and it applies the cheapest combination automatically (IFCN FAQ 2.2–2.3).

- PR1 is never included in the day, 3-day or 7-day rates, not even the Pedra Rija ticket (IFCN FAQ 2.4).

- The operator rate only applies when you book through a tour company that has a protocol with IFCN. Operators without one pay the normal rates (Portaria 48/2026 art. 4; IFCN FAQ 2.6).

- The Pedra Rija-only PR1 ticket (€4.50) is still on sale per IFCN and SIMplifica. The full PR1 ticket covers the PR1.1, PR1.2 and PR1.3 exits at no extra cost (IFCN FAQ 5.6).

## How much will my trip cost?

Enter what you plan to walk. The calculator applies the official 2026 rates and picks the cheapest combination, the way SIMplifica says it does.

An estimate from the official rates. It assumes your hiking days are in one run and all trails are in one SIMplifica booking. SIMplifica calculates the final price, and each trail still needs a free slot.

## Who pays nothing (but still books)

- Children aged 12 and under, visitors included, with proof of age.

- Residents of the Autonomous Region of Madeira, with a valid SIMplifica resident card plus citizen card or passport.

- People with a disability of 60% or more, and one guardian accompanying each of them, with proof.

- Athletes in events authorised by IFCN.

Exempt people must still be registered: book them on SIMplifica like everyone else (Portaria 48/2026 art. 9; IFCN FAQ 1.4, 2.7–2.9). Landowners along the trails and essential public services are outside the scheme altogether.

## Which walks need a ticket?

- IFCN-managed classified PR trails (PR1–PR1.3, PR2, PR5, PR6 and its branches, PR7 to PR22, PR27, PR28 and the three Porto Santo trails): booking and fee required.

- PR3 Vereda do Burro, PR3.1 Caminho Real do Monte and PR4 Levada do Barreiro (managed by the Funchal council) and PR23 Levada da Azenha (Caniço parish) are classified but not managed by IFCN: they are not on SIMplifica and carry no IFCN fee.

- Non-classified levadas and paths need no booking and no fee. IFCN doesn't maintain or recommend them.

Not sure about a particular walk? See Do I need a permit?

## Time slots, refunds and rescheduling

- Slots: you book a 30-minute entry window. IFCN allows about 15 minutes' tolerance either side, a little more if you are walking trails in sequence. It is an allowance, not a right.

- Booking: online only, on SIMplifica. Same-day and next-day booking work while slots remain. Nothing is sold at the trailhead or at IFCN offices.

- Refund or new date only if IFCN cancels (an official closure or restriction on your date). Email helpdesk.ifcn@madeira.gov.pt within 10 working days of the booked date and ask for a new date within a year on the same trail, or a full refund by bank transfer.

- Everything else loses the fee: rain, illness, a cancelled flight, a missed slot or a wrong date. The SIMplifica contact centre can't change or refund bookings.

## The fine for walking without a ticket

Walking an IFCN classified trail without a valid SIMplifica ticket is an administrative offence (contraordenação) under Portaria 801/2025, art. 10, and Decreto Legislativo Regional 24/2022/M, art. 13. The law sets fines for individuals of €250 to €2,500. Rangers may also ask you to leave the trail. Entering a closed trail carries the same fine range.

## What changed from 2025

The 2026 rates come from Portaria 801/2025, which revoked the earlier Portaria 556/2024. Under the old rules the standard fee was reported as €3 per trail; since 1 January 2026 it is €4.50, and booking a time slot is mandatory.

## Questions people ask

## How much does hiking in Madeira cost in 2026?

€4.50 per person for each classified PR trail managed by IFCN. PR1 costs €4.50 from Pico do Areeiro to the Pedra Rija viewpoint and back, or €10.50 for the full route to Pico Ruivo. Children 12 and under, Madeira residents and people with a disability of 60% or more pay nothing but must still book on SIMplifica.

## Are there day or multi-day hiking passes in Madeira?

There are combined rates, not passes: €9 for two or more trails in one day, €22.50 for two or more in 3 days and €52.50 for two or more in 7 days. PR1 is never included. Put all your trails in one SIMplifica booking and the cheapest combination is applied automatically; every trail still needs its own time slot.

## Is the fee cheaper with a tour operator?

Yes, if the operator has a protocol with IFCN: €3 per trail, €7 for the full PR1, and €6 / €15 / €35 for the day, 3-day and 7-day rates. Operators without a protocol pay the normal rates.

## Can I get a refund if it rains or I can't go?

No. The fee is refunded or moved to a new date only when IFCN officially closes or restricts the trail on your booked date. Email helpdesk.ifcn@madeira.gov.pt within 10 working days to ask for a new date within a year or a refund. Rain, illness or a cancelled flight don't qualify.

## What is the fine for hiking without a ticket in Madeira?

Walking an IFCN classified trail without a valid SIMplifica ticket is an administrative offence (Portaria 801/2025 art. 10; Decreto Legislativo Regional 24/2022/M art. 13). The law sets fines for individuals of €250 to €2,500.

## Do all levadas need a ticket?

No. Only classified PR trails managed by IFCN need a booking and fee. PR3, PR3.1, PR4 and PR23 are managed by the Funchal council or the Caniço parish and are not on SIMplifica. Non-classified levadas need no booking and no fee.

- Do I need a permit?: which walks need a ticket and which don't.

- Is PR1 open today?: the official status before you pay for a slot.

permit.text:
## Do I need a permit for levada walks in Madeira?

Everyone calls it a permit. Officially it's a timed booking (reserva) plus a fee (taxa), paid on the SIMplifica portal. Whether you need one depends on which kind of walk it is.

The short answer: you need a paid SIMplifica booking only for the classified PR trails managed by IFCN, the Region's forest and nature authority. That covers almost all the famous walks: PR1, PR6 25 Fontes, PR8 São Lourenço, PR9 Caldeirão Verde and more. Classified trails run by other bodies (PR3, PR3.1, PR4, PR23) and non-classified levadas need no booking and no IFCN fee.

## Three kinds of walk, three answers

## 1. IFCN classified PR trails Book + pay

35 trails on Madeira and 3 on Porto Santo. Before you walk, book a 30-minute entry slot and pay on SIMplifica: €4.50 per trail, €10.50 for the full PR1 (or €4.50 for Areeiro–Pedra Rija only). Carry the digital ticket; IFCN staff can ask for it.

How to book, step by step · All 2026 fees and passes

## 2. Classified trails run by someone else No IFCN fee

PR3 Vereda do Burro, PR3.1 Caminho Real do Monte and PR4 Levada do Barreiro are managed by the Câmara Municipal do Funchal; PR23 Levada da Azenha by the Junta de Freguesia do Caniço. IFCN's own list names these bodies as managers, and its FAQ (1.7) says a classified trail managed by another entity "is not available for booking on the Portal". They are not part of IFCN's booking system, so there is no IFCN fee.

## 3. Non-classified levadas and paths Free

Most of Madeira's levada network is not classified, for example Levada dos Tornos, Levada do Caniçal or Levada do Norte. There is nothing to book and nothing to pay (IFCN FAQ 1.7). But they are not classified, so they are not maintained or recommended by IFCN (FAQ 6.2): you walk them entirely at your own risk.

## What still applies

- Exempt people still book. Children 12 and under, Madeira residents, and people with a disability of 60% or more (plus one guardian) pay nothing, but they must be on the SIMplifica booking.

- Online only. There are no tickets at the trailhead or at IFCN offices. Same-day booking works if slots are left.

- No guide required. You can walk every PR trail on your own (IFCN FAQ 6.4).

- Closures apply to everyone. A booking doesn't open a closed trail, and a free levada can still be closed or dangerous. Check the live trail board: its status comes from the official IFCN warnings list and shows IFCN's own "updated" date.

Walking an IFCN classified trail without a valid SIMplifica ticket is an administrative offence (Portaria 801/2025 art. 10; DLR 24/2022/M art. 13); the law sets fines for individuals of €250–€2,500. Entering a closed trail is an offence under the same article.

## Questions people ask

## Do I need a permit to walk the levadas in Madeira?

Only on the classified PR trails managed by IFCN. For those you must book a timed entry slot and pay the fee on SIMplifica before you walk (€4.50 per trail, €10.50 for the full PR1). Classified trails run by other bodies (PR3, PR3.1, PR4, PR23) and non-classified levadas need no booking and no IFCN fee.

## Is it really a permit?

Not officially. It is a booking (reserva) of a 30-minute entry slot plus a fee (taxa), paid online on SIMplifica. The ticket is personal and valid for your date and slot. You don't need a guide.

## Which levada walks are free in Madeira?

PR3 Vereda do Burro, PR3.1 Caminho Real do Monte, PR4 Levada do Barreiro and PR23 Levada da Azenha are classified but managed by the Funchal council or the Caniço parish, so they aren't on SIMplifica and carry no IFCN fee. Non-classified levadas such as Levada dos Tornos need no booking either, but IFCN does not maintain or recommend them.

## My children are under 12. Do they need a booking?

Yes. Children 12 and under, residents and people with a disability of 60% or more don't pay, but they must still be included in the SIMplifica booking.

## What happens if I walk a PR trail without a ticket?

Walking an IFCN classified trail without a valid SIMplifica ticket is an administrative offence (Portaria 801/2025 art. 10; DLR 24/2022/M art. 13). The law sets fines for individuals of €250 to €2,500, and rangers may ask you to leave the trail.

## Why can't I find a trail on SIMplifica?

According to IFCN, a trail is missing from the portal when it is not classified, when it is classified but managed by another body (PR3, PR3.1, PR4, PR23), or when it is closed.

booking.text:
## How to book a Madeira trail on SIMplifica

Every classified PR trail managed by IFCN needs a timed booking on the Region's SIMplifica portal. Here are the steps, the rules on changes and refunds, and the traps.

The short answer: open the SIMplifica service “Pagamento de Taxas para acesso aos Percursos Pedestres Classificados”, log in, choose the trail, date and 30-minute entry slot, add every hiker (exempt ones too), pay by card, and keep the digital ticket that arrives by email. You can't change the booking for personal reasons; refunds happen only when IFCN closes the trail.

## Booking, step by step

- Open the service page. SIMplifica: trail fees service (portal home: simplifica.madeira.gov.pt). The portal is Portuguese-first, with a translate widget. Ver disponibilidade shows slot availability.

- Log in or create an account. An account is needed even for a single hiker. Do this at home a few days before, not at the trailhead.

- Choose the trail by its PR code. PR1 has two separate products: Pico do Areeiro ↔ Miradouro da Pedra Rija and back (€4.50, no access to Pico Ruivo), or the full one-way route Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo (€10.50, includes PR1.1 and PR1.2).

- Choose the date and 30-minute entry slot, then press Solicitar. Same-day and next-day bookings work if places are left. A full slot locks automatically.

- Add every hiker. Children 12 and under, Madeira residents and people with a disability of 60% or more (plus one guardian) pay nothing but must be on the booking. A tax number (NIF) is only needed if you want it on the invoice.

- Walking several trails? Put them all in one booking. There is no separate pass button: the day rate (€9), 3-day rate (€22.50) or 7-day rate (€52.50) is applied automatically at checkout. Each trail still gets its own slot, and PR1 is never included.

- Pay. The official methods are Multibanco (ATM reference), credit card and MB WAY. Multibanco and MB WAY need a Portuguese bank, so visitors pay by card.

- Keep the ticket. You get a payment receipt and a digital ticket by email, with the invoice. Show it at the trail, at control equipment, or when IFCN staff ask. Save it offline or print it: there is often no signal at the trailheads.

- On the day, arrive within your slot. IFCN allows a tolerance of about 15 minutes either side (a little more if you are doing trails in sequence). That is an allowance, not a right. For the full PR1, start at Pico do Areeiro, not at the Pedra Rija gate.

Prefer a video? SIMplifica has an official booking tutorial for visitors (EN).

## Changes, cancellations and refunds

- No changes for personal reasons. Rain, illness, a cancelled flight, the wrong date or a missed slot: you lose the full amount.

- When IFCN closes the trail on your date, email helpdesk.ifcn@madeira.gov.pt within 10 working days of the booked date. Ask for either a new date within one year (same trail, same group size, subject to availability) or a full refund.

- What to send: the tickets and invoice, plus the new date and slot you want, or for a refund a bank document with IBAN and SWIFT/BIC, the account holder's name and your address. Refunds are paid by bank transfer only.

- A weather warning doesn't close every trail automatically. Only an official closure counts.

- The SIMplifica Contact Center can't change or refund a paid booking.

## PR1: the Pedra Rija ticket can't be upgraded

A €4.50 “Pedra Rija” ticket covers only Pico do Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija and back. There is no conversion or upgrade: to walk on to Pico Ruivo you must buy a new €10.50 ticket, and the €4.50 isn't refunded. Check PR1's status today before choosing.

## Or let an operator book for you

Tour operators with an IFCN protocol book the trail for you at a lower fee: €3 per trail and €7 for the full PR1, instead of €4.50 and €10.50. Operators without a protocol pay the normal rates. Visit Madeira keeps a list of operators on its hiking page. All 2026 fees.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to do

| The portal won't load from abroad, or rejects your phone number | See SIMplifica from abroad: register with your email, turn off any VPN, try mobile data or another browser.

| The trail isn't in the list | It is not classified, it is managed by another body (PR3, PR3.1, PR4, PR23), or it is closed (IFCN FAQ 1.7). See which walks need a booking and the live board.

| A slot is greyed out | That slot's capacity is reached. Pick another time (FAQ 1.8).

| An email says your booking was “cancelled for inactivity / non-payment”, but you have tickets | It is usually an earlier, unfinished attempt. Compare the reference numbers; if they match your tickets, forward the email to IFCN.

| Card declined or portal errors | IFCN doesn't run the portal. Contact the SIMplifica Contact Center: +351 800 29 90 90, WhatsApp +351 926 155 465, 800299090@madeira.gov.pt (working days 9:00–18:00).

| Questions about the rules, reschedules or refunds | IFCN: +351 291 145 590, helpdesk.ifcn@madeira.gov.pt (working days 9:00–12:30 and 14:00–17:30).

## Questions people ask

## How do I book a trail on SIMplifica?

Open the SIMplifica service for classified trail fees, log in or create an account, choose the trail, the date and a 30-minute entry slot, add every hiker (including exempt ones), pay by card, and keep the digital ticket that arrives by email.

## Which payment methods does SIMplifica accept?

Multibanco (ATM reference), credit card and MB WAY. Multibanco and MB WAY need a Portuguese bank account, so visitors usually pay by card.

## Can I change or cancel my SIMplifica booking?

Not for personal reasons: rain, illness, a cancelled flight or a missed slot mean you lose the full amount. Only when IFCN cancels (for example an official closure on your date) can you ask for a new date within one year or a full refund.

## The trail is closed on my booked date. How do I get my money back?

Email helpdesk.ifcn@madeira.gov.pt within 10 working days of the booked date with your tickets and invoice. Ask for a new date and slot, or a refund by bank transfer (send IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, account holder's name and address).

## Can I upgrade a PR1 Pedra Rija ticket to the full route?

No. The €4.50 ticket covers only Pico do Areeiro to Pedra Rija and back. To continue to Pico Ruivo you need a new €10.50 ticket, and the first one is not refunded.

## How late can I arrive for my slot?

IFCN allows a tolerance of about 15 minutes either side of your entry slot, a little more if you are doing trails in sequence. It is an allowance, not a right.

## How do I get the 3-day or 7-day rate?

Put all your trails in one booking. There is no separate pass: the cheapest combination (€9 per day, €22.50 for 3 days, €52.50 for 7 days) is applied automatically. Each trail still needs its own slot, and PR1 is never included.

abroad.text:
## SIMplifica won't work from abroad?

Since 2026 the classified PR trails managed by IFCN need a booking through the government's SIMplifica portal (a few, such as PR3, PR3.1, PR4 and PR23, need no booking) — and that portal is the single biggest headache for visitors trying to plan from home.

The two-line fix: if the site won't take your phone number, register with your email instead — a foreign number isn't needed. If the site won't load at all, disable any VPN and try mobile data; if it still traps you, book once you land (it's reliable from a local connection) or have an operator hold your slot.

See also: the full SIMplifica booking guide: step by step, refunds and the PR1 ticket trap.

## What actually goes wrong — and the workaround

## Why won't the SIMplifica website open from my country? Access

SIMplifica is sometimes unreachable from outside Portugal — it loads the first screen then goes nowhere. Turn off any VPN (a foreign exit node can make it worse), try a different browser, or switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data. If it still won't complete, don't waste an evening on it: it works normally once you're on the island, or an operator can book for you.

## SIMplifica won't accept my phone number. What do I do? Registration

The portal frequently rejects non-Portuguese mobile numbers. Choose the email registration path instead of the phone one. Account type is "Pessoa Singular" (individual). Your password needs at least 10 characters using 3 of 4 types (upper, lower, number, symbol) — the "suggest strong password" button saves the hassle.

## Payment won't go through Checkout

Pay by credit or debit card (Visa or Mastercard) — that's the route that works for visitors. MB WAY and "ATM reference" are for Portuguese bank accounts, so skip them. Your ticket and QR code arrive by email, not SMS.

## Book before you fly — the calm version

- Create the account this week, from home, on the SIMplifica booking page — not on hike morning at the trailhead with no signal.

- Book the exact date and 30-minute entry slot. Slots have limited places and full ones lock; when PR1 reopened in May 2026, its first weekends sold out the day bookings opened.

- Screenshot the QR ticket. You may have to show it on the trail, at control equipment or when IFCN staff ask, and there's often no signal to reload your email.

- Everyone in the group goes on the booking — including under-12s (free) and residents (free) — or the whole reservation can be refused.

Walking an IFCN classified trail without a valid SIMplifica ticket is an administrative offence (Portaria 801/2025 art. 10; DLR 24/2022/M art. 13); the law sets fines for individuals of €250–€2,500. Same-day slots are possible if any remain, but a fixed travel date is a bad time to gamble on it.

## Can I book a Madeira trail after I arrive on the island? On the island

Yes: same-day and next-day booking is allowed if places remain, and the portal works normally from a local connection. But places are limited and full slots lock, so for a fixed date it is safer to book before you fly.

Sources: IFCN fees FAQ (booking, slots, tickets) · SIMplifica booking service · Portaria 801/2025 · Portaria 48/2026 (art. 7, showing your ticket) · DN Madeira, 29 Apr 2026 (PR1 sold out). Checked 30 Sep 2026.

back.text:
## How to get back from Pico Ruivo and Achada do Teixeira without a car

PR1 runs one-way, Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo, since the 1 May 2026 reopening, and you come down PR1.2 to Achada do Teixeira: a car park above Santana with no bus, far from where you started. Official prices checked September 2026.

No bus serves Achada do Teixeira, and walking PR1 back to Pico do Areeiro is not allowed. Sort your return before you start; phone signal at both ends is patchy.

## Which plan fits you

| Your situation | Plan | Cost

| No car, 3–4 people or on a budget | Public bus up to Pico do Areeiro (06:00 from Funchal) + a taxi booked to collect you at Achada do Teixeira | €3 pp bus + taxi: ask for a quote (metered taxi)

| No car, 1–2 people | Shared hiker transfer: dropped at Areeiro, collected at Achada | Ask for a quote; trail ticket usually extra

| Group of up to 8 | Private transfer: drop at Areeiro, pick-up at Achada | Ask for a quote

| Own car | Park at Pico do Areeiro, taxi from Achada back to your car | parking €4/h (upper car park) + taxi: ask for a quote (metered taxi)

| No transport plan | Skip the traverse: Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija there-and-back, or PR1.2 up and back from Achada | €4.50 ticket

## The public bus to Pico do Areeiro (the start only)

Horários do Funchal runs a "Pico do Areeiro" service every day except 25 December. It serves the start of PR1, not Achada do Teixeira, so it solves half the problem.

| Summer timetable (to 24 Oct 2026) | Morning | Afternoon

| Leaves Funchal, Teleférico terminus (stop 4A) | 06:00 | 13:30

| Arrives Pico do Areeiro (Radar roundabout) | 06:45 | 14:15

| Leaves Pico do Areeiro for Funchal | 12:15 | 19:00 (18:00 from 25 Oct)

- Fare €3.00 per trip, paid on board; other transport tickets aren't accepted. 31 seats.

- Seat reservations by phone only: 291 705 555, 7 to 2 working days before the trip (Mon–Thu 08:30–12:30 and 14:00–18:00, Fri 08:30–12:30 and 14:00–17:00). Be at the stop 15 minutes before departure.

- Summit shuttle between the CAM Florestal das Serras de Santo António stop, the Pico do Areeiro car park and the Radar roundabout: every 15 minutes, 06:40–12:15 and 14:10–19:00 (18:00 in winter), €1.20, runs with at least 4 passengers.

The 06:45 arrival is before sunrise all year (only just, in June and July). It works for a sunrise start, or for a Pedra Rija there-and-back with the 12:15 bus down. For the full traverse you still need someone to collect you at Achada. More in sunrise transport to Pico do Areeiro.

## Taxis from Achada do Teixeira

Taxis don't wait at Achada do Teixeira. Book one for a set pick-up time before you start, or call from the trail end if you have signal. Save the number first.

- Táxis Santana: +351 291 572 540 (the rank nearest Achada do Teixeira)

- Táxis Funchal: +351 291 764 476

Numbers as printed on IFCN's trailhead panels (the PR1.1 and PR1.2 panels for Santana). Whether each line is staffed today isn't verified.

What it costs: taxis charge by the meter at the official regulated tariff, set by the Region's transport authority (IMT-RAM) with the taxi associations and in force since 1 January 2026. There is no fixed price per route; nights, weekends and holidays cost more. Ask for a quote when you book.

Compare two quotes: call the rank nearest the pick-up (Táxis Santana +351 291 572 540 for Achada do Teixeira) and a Funchal taxi (Táxis Madeira +351 291 764 476, online booking at taxismadeira.pt; AITRAM +351 291 765 760, both listed by Visit Madeira). Ask each for a quote for the whole trip and take the better one.

If you need a ride-hailing app in Madeira, your option is Bolt. Taxis are available from Funchal, Santana and other towns (numbers above).

## Cheaper: a taxi down to Santana, then the bus

No bus reaches Achada do Teixeira, but Santana, down the road, has CAM buses to Funchal. Book a taxi from Achada do Teixeira to Santana only (a much shorter ride than all the way to Funchal; ask the fare when you book) and take the bus from there.

Santana → Funchal. Monday to Friday: 11:00 (route 801, in Funchal 12:30, or route 885, 12:40), 12:30 (801, 14:25) and 17:25 (860, 19:00). Saturdays: 12:00 (801, 13:30), 13:15 (860, 14:20) and 17:28 (860, 19:20). Sundays and holidays: 15:30 (801, 16:50) and 17:28 (860, 19:20).

Times as printed on CAM's Santana network timetable; times at intermediate stops are approximate and can change with traffic or bad weather. No buses on 25 December. Check before you travel with CAM: info@cam-madeira.pt, +351 291 201 150.

## Transfers and other options

## Shared hiker transfer 1–2 people

A minibus drops you at Pico do Areeiro (often before sunrise) and collects you at Achada do Teixeira at a set time. Prices vary, so ask for a quote. The trail ticket is usually extra: €10.50 on SIMplifica, or €7 when an operator with an IFCN protocol books it. Examples: Beyond Madeira, Doit Madeira, Pico Transfers, GetToHikes. Book the day before at the latest; sunrise pick-ups fill up.

## Private transfer Groups

Your own vehicle, drop at Areeiro and pick-up at Achada. One seller, madeira.best, offers it for up to 8 people; ask for a quote. Shared between 4–8 people it can cost less per head than shared seats.

## Guided tour with transport Zero logistics

IFCN protocol operators bundle the ticket (€7 on PR1), a guide and both transfers. The most expensive option, but closures and sold-out slots become their problem.

## Two cars Groups

Leave one car at Achada do Teixeira and drive the other to Pico do Areeiro. It costs an hour of shuttling plus Areeiro parking (€4/h in the upper car park).

Walking PR1 back from Pico Ruivo to Pico do Areeiro is not permitted: beyond Pedra Rija the route is one-way. Rangers are on the trail.

## Before you go

- Check today's PR1 status. It comes from IFCN's official warnings list and shows IFCN's own "updated" date. Your SIMplifica slot has rules about rescheduling.

- Screenshot your ticket. Signal on the ridge is unreliable and rangers do check.

- Set the pick-up time with margin: Visit Madeira gives about 3 hours for Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo, then allow about an hour down PR1.2 to Achada do Teixeira, more with photo stops.

## Questions

## Is there a bus from Achada do Teixeira?

No. No regular bus serves Achada do Teixeira; the nearest bus services are down in Santana. The only public bus in the area is Horários do Funchal's Pico do Areeiro service (€3), which serves the start of PR1, not the end. Arrange a taxi or transfer to collect you.

## How much is a taxi from Achada do Teixeira to Pico do Areeiro or Funchal?

There is no fixed price per route. Taxis charge by the meter at the official tariff set by the Region's transport authority (IMT-RAM) with the taxi associations, in force since 1 January 2026; nights, weekends and holidays cost more. Ask for a quote when you book, and book ahead for a set pick-up time; Táxis Santana is on +351 291 572 540 (the number on IFCN's trailhead panels).

## Is there a bus to Pico do Areeiro?

Yes. Horários do Funchal's Pico do Areeiro service leaves Funchal (Teleférico terminus) at 06:00 and 13:30 every day except 25 December, arriving at 06:45 and 14:15, and comes back down at 12:15 and 19:00 (18:00 in winter). The fare is €3.00, paid on board; seats can be reserved on 291 705 555.

## Can I walk back from Pico Ruivo to Pico do Areeiro?

No. Since the 1 May 2026 reopening the full route is one-way, Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo. Only the 1.2 km Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija section is two-way. From Pico Ruivo you go down PR1.2 to Achada do Teixeira.

## How much does a shared hiker transfer cost?

Prices vary by company and group size, so ask for a quote when you book. The trail ticket is usually extra: €10.50 on SIMplifica, or €7 if an operator with an IFCN protocol books it.

Sources: Horários do Funchal, Pico do Areeiro service · IFCN warnings list · IFCN trail list and trailhead panels · Portaria 48/2026 (fees) · DN on Areeiro parking · IMT-RAM, Primeira alteração à Convenção n.º 1/2019 (taxi tariff) · Visit Madeira, taxis.

sunrise.text:
## Getting to Pico do Areeiro for sunrise: bus, transfer, taxi or car

A neutral comparison for PR1 hikers and sunrise watchers. Official prices checked September 2026, with sources. No affiliate links, nothing for sale.

Short answer: the cheapest way up is the public 06:00 bus from Funchal (€3). It reaches Pico do Areeiro at 06:45, before sunrise every day of the year. It doesn't go to Achada do Teixeira, where the full one-way PR1 ends, so for the full traverse you also need a transfer or taxi back. Shared sunrise transfers can handle both ends; prices vary, so ask for a quote.

Sunrise at Pico do Areeiro today: about – (from the summit with a clear horizon about –), Madeira time.

## The options side by side

Official prices checked September 2026. Per person unless stated.

| Option | Price | Sunrise timing | Back from Achada do Teixeira?

| Public bus “Pico do Areeiro” (Horários do Funchal) | €3.00 per trip, paid on board | Funchal (Teleférico stop) 06:00 → summit 06:45: before sunrise all year | No. Down from the summit at 12:15 and 19:00 (18:00 from 25 Oct 2026)

| Shared sunrise transfer | Ask for a quote; PR1 ticket usually extra | Pick-ups about 05:40–06:30 (one operator's Sept 2026 schedule) | Yes, most collect at Achada around 12:30–12:50

| Private transfer | Ask for a quote | Pick-up about 1 h 30 before sunrise | Yes, if you book the Achada pick-up

| Taxi | Ask for a quote (metered taxi) | Any time you book | Only if arranged in advance; taxis don't wait at Achada

| Own or hire car | Parking €4.00/hour at the upper car park (first 15 min free) | Arrive well before sunrise; spaces are limited | No: the car stays at Areeiro, so you need a lift back to it

Bus and parking prices are the official published ones. Taxi and transfer prices vary, so ask for a quote before you book. Levadinho has no commercial link with any company named here.

## PR1 the public bus in detail

Horários do Funchal runs a named service, “Pico do Areeiro”, every day except 25 December. The summer timetable runs until 24 October 2026; the winter timetable from 25 October 2026 to 27 March 2027.

- Up: 06:00 and 13:30 from the Teleférico terminus stop (4A) in Funchal, via Monte, Terreiro da Luta and Poiso, arriving at the Radar roundabout at Pico do Areeiro at 06:45 and 14:15.

- Down: 12:15 and 19:00 from the Radar roundabout (18:00 instead of 19:00 in winter), back at the Teleférico at 13:00 and 19:45.

- Fare: €3.00 per trip, bought on board. No other transport tickets are accepted. 31 seats.

- Seat reservations by phone only, 7 to 2 working days before the trip: 291 705 555 (Mon–Thu 08:30–12:30 and 14:00–18:00, Fri 08:30–12:30 and 14:00–17:00). With a reservation, be at the stop 15 minutes before departure.

- Summit shuttle: €1.20 per trip, every 15 minutes (06:40–12:15 and 14:10–19:00, 18:00 in winter), between the CAM Florestal das Serras de Santo António, the Pico do Areeiro car park and the Radar roundabout. It leaves with at least 4 passengers.

Sunrise margin: the 06:45 arrival beats sunrise every day of the year, but in June and early July only by about 8–15 minutes (table below). The stop is the Radar roundabout, a short walk from the viewpoint. The bus doesn't serve Achada do Teixeira, so it suits sunrise only, an out-and-back to Pedra Rija (€4.50 ticket, back on the 12:15), or the way up if a transfer or taxi collects you at the end.

## Shared and private transfers

Several companies run shared vans that drop hikers at Pico do Areeiro before sunrise and collect them at Achada do Teixeira after the traverse. Prices vary, so ask for a quote. This is what their own pages said on 30 September 2026:

- Beyond Madeira: shared, up to 9 people, pay on the day, free cancellation up to 48 h; collects at Achada do Teixeira. The page is unclear about whether the trail ticket is included, so ask.

- Doit Madeira: a PR1 + PR1.2 sunrise transfer; it can also sell you the PR1 ticket at €7.

- Pico Transfers: September 2026 schedule: pick-up 05:40–06:30 in Funchal/Caniço, collection at Achada do Teixeira 12:30–12:50, drop-off 13:30–14:30. The €10.50 ticket is not included.

- GetToHikes: sunrise transfer with pick-ups at Ajuda, Lido and central Funchal; no price in the page text.

- Marketplaces such as GetYourGuide and Booking.com list similar shared transfers.

- Private: madeira.best offers a sunrise round trip to Areeiro by car (up to 3) or minivan (4–8), or a drop at Areeiro with collection at Achada do Teixeira, with hotel pick-up about 1 h 30 before sunrise.

Why some quote €7 for the ticket and others €10.50: IFCN protocol operators pay the operator rate for PR1, €7, set by Portaria 48/2026. On your own it is €10.50 on SIMplifica. See hiking fees 2026.

## Taxi or your own car

- Taxi: taxis charge by the meter at the official regulated tariff, set by the Region's transport authority (IMT-RAM) with the taxi associations and in force since 1 January 2026. There is no fixed price per route; nights, weekends and holidays cost more, so ask for a quote when you book. Taxis don't wait at Achada do Teixeira: agree a pick-up time. Call the rank nearest the pick-up (Táxis Santana +351 291 572 540 for Achada do Teixeira, the number printed on IFCN's trailhead panels) and a Funchal taxi (Táxis Madeira +351 291 764 476, online booking at taxismadeira.pt; AITRAM +351 291 765 760, both listed by Visit Madeira). Ask each for a quote for the whole trip and take the better one.

- Own or hire car: the upper car park at the summit costs €4.00 per hour (first 15 minutes free; about 70 spaces). A lower car park with about 300 spaces was announced at €2 per hour (DN, 2024). Car parks fill up at sunrise, so arrive early. The catch is PR1's one-way rule: your car stays at Areeiro while you finish at Achada do Teixeira, so you need a taxi or transfer back to it.

If you need a ride-hailing app in Madeira, your option is Bolt. Taxis are available from Funchal, Santana and other towns (numbers above).

## Sunrise times and SIMplifica slots

Sunrise at Pico do Areeiro on the 1st of each month, Madeira time. Computed; accurate to about ±2 min. Clocks change on the last Sundays of March and October.

| Month | Sunrise | Summit, clear horizon | 06:45 bus arrives … min before

| January | 08:10 | 08:03 | 78

| February | 08:03 | 07:56 | 71

| March | 07:36 | 07:30 | 45

| April | 07:56 | 07:50 | 65

| May | 07:21 | 07:15 | 30

| June | 07:01 | 06:54 | 9

| July | 07:03 | 06:57 | 12

| August | 07:21 | 07:15 | 30

| September | 07:42 | 07:36 | 51

| October | 08:02 | 07:56 | 71

| November | 07:25 | 07:19 | 34

| December | 07:52 | 07:45 | 60

- Sunrise slots at 07:00 and 07:30 were added in June 2026 for sunrise demand, 70 places each from 21 June (Diário de Notícias, 19 June 2026). Slots are 30 minutes with about 15 minutes' tolerance (IFCN FAQ 1.3).

- From mid-May to late July the sun rises around 07:00, so a 07:00 slot lets you watch it and set off straight away.

- The rest of the year it rises later, up to about 08:10 in early January and mid-October. To watch it from the viewpoint before you start, book a slot that begins after sunrise (for example 08:00 or 08:30 in October). An earlier slot means starting the ridge in the dark.

- Booking step by step: how to book on SIMplifica.

## Do you need a ticket just to watch the sunrise?

The fee is charged for entering the classified trail (Portaria 48/2026, arts. 5–6). The Pico do Areeiro viewpoint is by the car park, outside the trail, so watching the sunrise there should not need a ticket. We haven't found an official statement that says so explicitly, so check with IFCN if in doubt.

Once you walk onto PR1, you need a valid SIMplifica ticket for your slot. Walking an IFCN classified trail without one is an administrative offence (Portaria 801/2025 art. 10; DLR 24/2022/M art. 13), and the law sets fines for individuals of €250–€2,500.

## The one-way finish: plan the way back first

PR1 status comes from the official IFCN warnings list and carries IFCN's own “updated” date. It loads here as a live badge (needs JavaScript).

Since the full route reopened on 1 May 2026, PR1 beyond Pedra Rija is one-way: Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo, then down PR1.2 to Achada do Teixeira. No bus serves Achada do Teixeira, and IFCN says hikers are responsible for their own transport (IFCN FAQ 5.5). So there are two halves to plan: getting up for sunrise, and getting back from Achada around midday. When only Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija is open (see the card above), it's an out-and-back and the bus works both ways.

→ Getting back from PR1: every option for the return.

## Sunrise transport: questions

## Is there a bus to Pico do Areeiro for sunrise?

Yes. Horários do Funchal's “Pico do Areeiro” bus leaves the Teleférico stop in Funchal at 06:00 and reaches the summit at 06:45, before sunrise every day of the year. It costs €3.00 per trip, paid on board, and runs daily except 25 December. Seats can be reserved by phone on 291 705 555, 7 to 2 working days ahead (checked September 2026).

## How much is a PR1 sunrise transfer?

Shared and private hiker transfers run to Pico do Areeiro for sunrise; prices vary, so ask for a quote when you book. The PR1 ticket is usually extra: €10.50 on SIMplifica, or €7 if the operator books it. Taxis charge by the meter at the official tariff, with no fixed price per route.

## Do I need a SIMplifica ticket just to watch the sunrise at Pico do Areeiro?

The fee applies to entering the classified trail, and the viewpoint is by the car park, outside it, so watching the sunrise there should not need a ticket. We found no explicit official statement, so check with IFCN if unsure. Walking onto PR1 needs a valid ticket for your slot.

## Which PR1 slot should I book for sunrise?

Slots at 07:00 and 07:30 were added in June 2026 for sunrise demand. From mid-May to late July the sun rises around 07:00, so the 07:00 slot fits. The rest of the year sunrise is later (up to about 08:10), so pick a slot that starts after sunrise if you want to watch it from the viewpoint first.

## How do I get back from Achada do Teixeira after PR1?

No bus serves Achada do Teixeira. Book a transfer that collects you there, or arrange a taxi in advance (Táxis Santana +351 291 572 540, as printed on IFCN panels). Taxis charge by the meter at the official tariff, with no fixed price per route, so ask for a quote when you book.

## Is PR1 one-way? Yes: Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo only

The 2026 rule on one page, checked on 2 October 2026 against IFCN, Visit Madeira and SIMplifica. Pico do Arieiro and Pico do Areeiro are the same summit.

Yes. Since the full route reopened on 1 May 2026, PR1 is one-way beyond the Pedra Rija viewpoint, in the direction Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo. You can't walk it from Pico Ruivo back to Areeiro. From Pico Ruivo you go down PR1.2 to Achada do Teixeira (or PR1.1 to Ilha), and no bus serves Achada do Teixeira. The one-way section opened Friday to Sunday at first and has been open daily since 26 June 2026. The first 1.2 km, Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija, is still two-way.

## Is the one-way section open today?

IFCN closes the Pedra Rija – Pico Ruivo section on some days for scheduled works (it did on 14–17 and 21–22 September 2026), while Areeiro ↔ Pedra Rija stays open both ways. The card below shows IFCN's own listing and its date. If the IFCN warnings list and Visit Madeira's PR1 page disagree, check both before you go.

→ Is PR1 open today? Live status, sold-out fixes and rescheduling.

Trail status comes from the official IFCN warnings list, which IFCN updates when conditions change and dates itself ("updated"). It is shown here as a live badge (it needs JavaScript). If it doesn't appear, check the official sources linked below.

## What is one-way, and what isn't

Distances from IFCN and Visit Madeira. Directions from IFCN FAQ 5.3–5.4.

| Section | Distance | Direction | Ticket

| Pico do Areeiro ↔ Miradouro da Pedra Rija | 1.2 km each way | Two-way: out-and-back allowed | €4.50 Pedra Rija ticket

| Miradouro da Pedra Rija → Pico Ruivo | rest of the 6.1 km route | One-way, towards Pico Ruivo only | €10.50 full ticket

| Pico Ruivo → Achada do Teixeira (PR1.2) | 2.8 km | The usual way down | Included in the €10.50

| Pico Ruivo → Ilha (PR1.1 Vereda da Ilha) | 8.2 km | The other way down | Included in the €10.50

- The full route starts at Pico do Areeiro, not at the Pedra Rija gate: enter in the Areeiro area at your slot time (IFCN FAQ 5.2).

- There is no way back along PR1 once you pass Pedra Rija: Visit Madeira describes the full route as one-way "with no possibility of returning along the same path".

- PR1 follows the west variant through the tunnels. The east variant over Pico das Torres is listed as closed (IFCN trail list).

- Want Pico Ruivo without the one-way logistics? PR1.2 from Achada do Teixeira is a separate trail that IFCN lists as 2.8 km plus 2.8 km back.

## Why is it one-way?

The official texts state the rule but not the reason. IFCN's FAQ (5.3) only says that from Pedra Rija "the trail operates on a one-way basis, in the direction Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo", and the Regional Government announced it together with the reopening (JM). The section beyond Pedra Rija had been closed since a rockfall caused by the August 2024 wildfire, and repair work carried on after the reopening. Some tour and blog sites say one-way traffic eases crowding on the narrow ridge; that is their explanation, not an official one.

## Which ticket: €10.50 or €4.50?

- Full traverse, Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo: €10.50 on SIMplifica. SIMplifica sells it as "exclusivamente unidirecional" (one-way only), and it includes PR1.1 and PR1.2 for the way down.

- Areeiro – Pedra Rija and back: €4.50. SIMplifica's own wording: two-way to the Pedra Rija viewpoint at km 1.2, and it "does not give access to Pico Ruivo".

- Through an IFCN protocol operator, the full PR1 costs €7 (Portaria 48/2026).

- No upgrades: a €4.50 ticket can't be converted. To go on to Pico Ruivo you need a new €10.50 ticket, and the €4.50 isn't refunded (IFCN FAQ 5.7–5.8).

- Children aged 12 and under, residents and people with a disability of 60% or more are exempt, but must still be on the booking. PR1 is not part of the day or multi-day rates.

How to book on SIMplifica (step by step, and the Pedra Rija trap) · Hiking fees 2026

## Plan the way back before you book

Because PR1 is one-way, you finish at Achada do Teixeira, far from your start. No bus serves Achada do Teixeira, and IFCN says hikers are responsible for their own transport (IFCN FAQ 5.5). If you drove to Areeiro, your car stays there.

- Shared hiker transfer that drops you at Areeiro and collects you at Achada: prices vary, so ask for a quote.

- Taxi, booked in advance: taxis don't wait at Achada. Taxis charge by the meter at the official tariff set by the Region's transport authority (IMT-RAM) with the taxi associations (in force since 1 January 2026); there is no fixed price per route, and nights, weekends and holidays cost more. Call the rank nearest the pick-up (Táxis Santana +351 291 572 540, as printed on IFCN's trailhead panels) and a Funchal taxi (Táxis Madeira +351 291 764 476, online booking at taxismadeira.pt; AITRAM +351 291 765 760, both listed by Visit Madeira). Ask each for a quote for the whole trip and take the better one.

→ Getting back from PR1: every option. → PR1 sunrise transport: bus, transfer, taxi or car to the start.

## PR1 one-way: questions

## Is PR1 Pico do Areeiro one-way?

Yes. Since the full route reopened on 1 May 2026, PR1 is one-way from the Pedra Rija viewpoint to Pico Ruivo, in the direction Pico do Areeiro → Pico Ruivo. Only the first 1.2 km, between Pico do Areeiro and Pedra Rija, is still two-way. You finish by going down from Pico Ruivo to Achada do Teixeira (PR1.2) or to Ilha (PR1.1).

## Can I hike PR1 from Pico Ruivo to Pico do Areeiro?

No. IFCN only allows the section between Pedra Rija and Pico Ruivo in the direction of Pico Ruivo, so you can't start at Pico Ruivo or Achada do Teixeira and walk to Pico do Areeiro, and you can't walk the whole route there and back.

## Can I walk from Pico do Areeiro to Pedra Rija and back?

Yes. Pico do Areeiro – Pedra Rija viewpoint (1.2 km each way) is still two-way. It has its own €4.50 SIMplifica ticket, which does not let you continue to Pico Ruivo.

## Since when has PR1 been one-way?

Since the full reopening on 1 May 2026. The one-way section first opened Friday to Sunday only, because of surface repairs, and has been open every day since 26 June 2026. IFCN still closes it on some days for works, so check the live status before you go.

## Why is PR1 one-way?

IFCN and the Regional Government state the rule but have not published a reason in the texts we checked. The rule came with the reopening after repairs to the rockfall caused by the August 2024 wildfire. The crowding explanation found on some tour sites is not an official one.

## How do I get back after hiking PR1 one-way?

No bus serves Achada do Teixeira, and IFCN does not arrange the return. Book a transfer that collects you at Achada do Teixeira, or arrange a taxi in advance (Táxis Santana +351 291 572 540, as printed on IFCN panels). Taxis charge by the meter at the official tariff, with no fixed price per route, so ask for a quote when you book.

What the summit is doing right now: the live webcam, the latest measured reading from IPMA's weather station at the top (~1,800 m), the difference with Funchal, and today's sunrise. We don't forecast; we show what's measured and link to the forecasts.
