The live readings need JavaScript. You can read IPMA's hourly station data directly on the IPMA website (station “Madeira, Pico do Areeiro”).

Sunrise and sunset are computed for Pico do Areeiro (32.735° N, 16.928° W), Madeira time, standard horizon, accurate to about ±2 minutes. From the summit, with a clear eastern horizon (sea or cloud tops), the sun shows about 6 minutes earlier.

## Live webcam: Pico do Arieiro summit

Webcam: NetMadeira · refresh the page for a new frame
Full-size webcam ↗

The camera belongs to NetMadeira and is embedded with its own share code. It pans between the Pico do Areeiro viewpoint, the start of the PR1 path, Ninho da Manta, Pico do Cidrão and the observatory. It is sometimes offline or shows a placeholder; then try the NetMadeira timelapses or the same camera on Windy.

## Is PR1 open today?

PR1 status comes from the official IFCN warnings list and carries IFCN's own “updated” date. It loads here as a live badge (needs JavaScript).

A clear webcam doesn't mean the trail is open, and bad weather doesn't close it automatically: IFCN decides closures case by case (IFCN FAQ 4.2). Details, sold-out fixes and sunrise slots: PR1 today.

## When is it clear? The sea of clouds, honestly

Pico do Areeiro is one of the foggiest places on Madeira: it averages 229 fog days a year (INMG 1979, cited in Prada et al. 2009). The north-east trade winds push moist air against the island's east–west mountain barrier, so cloud builds on the north side, usually between about 600–800 m and 1,600 m.

A warm layer above it, the trade-wind temperature inversion, puts a lid on that cloud (mechanism). That is why the peaks at about 1,800 m can stand above a flat “sea of clouds” while Funchal is grey. But the summit is also often inside the cloud, and nobody measures how often the sea of clouds forms at Areeiro, so we don't give odds.

- Rule of thumb, not a forecast: summit humidity below about 90 % means the station is probably out of the cloud; 90 % or more usually means you're in it.

- The webcam is the real test. Look before you drive up, and again before you set off.

- It rains a lot up here: about 2,928 mm a year at Areeiro against about 513 mm in Funchal.

## Cold, frost, snow and wind

- Much colder than Funchal. On the 24 hours we sampled (29–30 September 2026), IPMA measured the summit 8.8–13.8 °C colder than Funchal, most of all around dawn. On inversion days the gap can shrink. The tiles above show the latest pair.

- Frost and snow happen. The summit dropped to −3.3 °C on 19 March 2026 (DN) and snow whitened the highest peaks on 7 April 2026 (DN).

- Wind. We flag strong wind from 40 km/h. There is no official IFCN wind limit. The summit wind sensor is often out of action; when it is, we show the reading from IPMA's lower Areeiro station, about 2 km away.

- IFCN's own trail panels say: “Weather subject to frequent changes, take warm clothing.”

## Forecasts (we don't make one)

Everything above is a measured observation or an astronomical calculation. For what's coming, use a forecast:

- IPMA forecast by place: the official Portuguese weather service (pick Madeira).

- IPMA weather warnings: yellow/orange/red warnings for the Madeira mountains.

- Windy for wind and cloud models at the summit; mountain-forecast.com (Pico do Arieiro, 1,818 m); meteoblue.

## Pico do Areeiro weather: questions

## Is there a live webcam at Pico do Areeiro (Arieiro)?

Yes. NetMadeira runs a live camera at the summit that pans between the viewpoint, the start of the PR1 path and the nearby peaks. It is embedded on this page with NetMadeira's own share code, and the same camera is on Windy. It is sometimes offline.

## How much colder is Pico do Areeiro than Funchal?

Often around 10–14 °C colder, though it varies with the weather. Over 29–30 September 2026 IPMA measured the summit 8.8–13.8 °C colder than Funchal. The summit has had frost (−3.3 °C on 19 March 2026) and snow (7 April 2026). This page shows the latest measured pair.

## Will I see a sea of clouds at sunrise?

Nobody can promise it. The trade-wind inversion often keeps the cloud below the peaks, but Pico do Areeiro itself averages 229 fog days a year. Check the webcam and the summit humidity before you go: below about 90 % the station is probably out of the cloud.

## What time is sunrise at Pico do Areeiro?

Between about 06:59 in mid-June and 08:10 in early January (Madeira time), and around 08:00 in early October. This page computes today's time. From the summit, with a clear eastern horizon, the sun shows about 6 minutes earlier.

## Is this a weather forecast?

No. The readings are IPMA's measured hourly observations from its Pico do Areeiro station. For a forecast, use IPMA, Windy or a mountain forecast; the links are on this page.

- Getting to Pico do Areeiro for sunrise: bus, transfer, taxi or car, compared.

- Getting back from PR1: the one-way finish at Achada do Teixeira.

free.text:
## Free walks in Madeira: which levadas need no ticket?

Since 2026 the famous PR trails cost €4.50 and need a timed booking. Many other walks cost nothing. Here is what the official sources actually say.

The short answer: only the classified PR trails managed by IFCN need a paid SIMplifica ticket: €4.50 per trail, €10.50 for the full PR1. Every walk outside that list needs no ticket. That means the non-classified levadas and paths (for example Levada dos Tornos, Levada do Caniçal, Levada do Norte) and the four classified trails run by other bodies: PR3, PR3.1, PR4 and PR23 (IFCN FAQ 1.7 and 2.5).

## Free, or ticket needed? The rule in three lines

- IFCN classified PR trails: ticket needed. Book a 30-minute slot and pay on SIMplifica before you walk. This covers almost every famous walk: PR1, PR6 25 Fontes, PR8 São Lourenço, PR9 Caldeirão Verde, PR11 Balcões and more.

- Classified trails run by someone else: no IFCN ticket. PR3, PR3.1 and PR4 are managed by the Câmara Municipal do Funchal, PR23 by the Junta de Freguesia do Caniço. IFCN says such trails are not on the booking portal. We found no charge of their own.

- Non-classified levadas and paths: nothing to book, nothing to pay. But IFCN does not maintain, signpost or recommend them (FAQ 6.2, 6.3).

One catch: if a free walk joins or crosses an IFCN PR trail, the stretch on that PR trail needs a ticket. IFCN tells hikers to check whether their own itinerary passes through any PR it manages (FAQ 6.3).

## Walks with no ticket

Only walks the official sources (or our verified facts files) support. The live badge shows the official IFCN status where the walk is, or overlaps, a PR trail; hover or tap it for IFCN's note.

| PR3.1 Caminho Real do Monte… | Ribeira das Cales – Monte, 5.5 km | Classified PR, run by Funchal council | Not on SIMplifica; no IFCN fee. Continues PR3 down to Monte. | IFCN list

| PR4 Levada do Barreiro… | Poço da Neve – Casa do Barreiro, 6.7 km | Classified PR, run by Funchal council | Not on SIMplifica; no IFCN fee. IFCN lists the current route as Poço da Neve – Levada do Barreiro – Ribeira das Cales. | IFCN list

| PR23 Levada da Azenha | Azenha – Caminho Velho do Castelo (Caniço), 1.3 km | Classified PR, run by Caniço parish | Not on SIMplifica; no IFCN fee. Not on our live board: check the IFCN list. | IFCN list · see IFCN list

| Levada dos Tornos | Hills above Funchal, e.g. near Camacha | Non-classified levada | Not on IFCN's classified list or on SIMplifica. ⚠ One third-party site calls it “PR29” with a €4.50 fee; IFCN's list has no PR29. | IFCN FAQ 1.7 · location · madeirahiking.org

| Levada do NortePR17: … | Several sections | Non-classified levada | Free where it runs on its own, but one stretch is part of PR17 Caminho do Pináculo e Folhadal, which needs a ticket. | IFCN FAQ 1.7 · Visit Madeira PR17

| Levada Nova | Lombada church, Ponta do Sol (loop start) | Non-classified levada | Not an official PR route, so not on SIMplifica. Several levadas carry the name “Levada Nova”. The popular loop combines it with a “Levada do Moinho”: if your route uses IFCN's PR7 Levada do Moinho, that part needs a ticket. | IFCN FAQ 1.7 · location

## Often asked, but not free

## PR7 Levada do Moinho …

PR7 Levada do Moinho (Ribeira da Cruz – Lamaceiros) is a classified trail managed by IFCN, so it needs a €4.50 SIMplifica ticket whenever it is open.

## What still applies

- Exempt doesn't mean unbooked. On IFCN trails, children 12 and under, Madeira residents and people with a disability of 60% or more (plus one guardian) pay nothing, but they must still be on the SIMplifica booking.

- Free walks are not checked like IFCN trails. IFCN is not responsible for the maintenance, signage or safety of non-classified trails (FAQ 6.3) and cannot recommend them (FAQ 6.2). They are not on IFCN's warnings list, so our live board can't show their status.

- Closures apply to everyone. PR3, PR3.1, PR4 and PR23 are on the IFCN list with their own status. Entering a closed trail is an offence, ticket or not.

Walking an IFCN classified trail without a valid SIMplifica ticket is an administrative offence (Portaria 801/2025 art. 10; DLR 24/2022/M art. 13); the law sets fines for individuals of €250–€2,500. Entering a closed trail is an offence under the same article.

## Questions

## Are any levada walks in Madeira free?

Yes. Only the classified PR trails managed by IFCN need a paid SIMplifica ticket (€4.50 per trail, €10.50 for the full PR1). Non-classified levadas such as Levada dos Tornos, Levada do Caniçal and Levada do Norte, and the classified trails run by other bodies (PR3, PR3.1, PR4 and PR23), need no IFCN booking and no IFCN fee.

## Is Levada Nova free?

Levada Nova is not an official PR route, so it is not on SIMplifica and needs no ticket. Guides often combine it with a “Levada do Moinho”: any part of your route on an IFCN PR trail, such as PR7 Levada do Moinho, needs a ticket. IFCN does not maintain or recommend non-classified levadas.

## Is Levada do Moinho free?

No. PR7 Levada do Moinho (Ribeira da Cruz – Lamaceiros) is a classified trail managed by IFCN, so it needs a €4.50 ticket on SIMplifica. Check its live badge on this page before you plan.

## Do I need SIMplifica for PR3, PR3.1, PR4 or PR23?

No. IFCN's list names the Funchal council (PR3, PR3.1, PR4) and the Caniço parish (PR23) as their managers, and IFCN says trails managed by another body are not on the booking portal. There is no IFCN fee, and we found no charge from those bodies either.

## Do children need a ticket?

On IFCN trails, children 12 and under, residents and people with a disability of 60% or more don't pay, but they must still be on the SIMplifica booking. On the free walks there is nothing to book.

## What happens if I walk a paid trail without a ticket?

Walking an IFCN classified trail without a valid SIMplifica ticket is an administrative offence (Portaria 801/2025 art. 10; DLR 24/2022/M art. 13). The law sets fines for individuals of €250 to €2,500.

## Levadas by bus: which trails can you reach without a car?

Times from the operators' timetables on SIGA, the Region's public transport site. Each trail's page has the full list.

The short answer: four trails have a bus to the start and back from the end: PR8 São Lourenço, PR11 Balcões, PR19 and PR20. For PR9 Caldeirão Verde you take the bus to Santana and a taxi up. Six more have a bus at one end only. No bus reaches Rabaçal (25 Fontes), the Paul da Serra plateau or the Fanal.

## There and back by bus

## PR8 Vereda da Ponta de São Lourenço …

Getting there. Baía d'Abra, where the walk starts and ends, is a bus stop. CAM line 113 (new no. 702), Funchal → Baía d'Abra, first bus: Monday to Friday 07:30 → 08:50; Saturdays 07:30 → 08:45; Sundays and holidays 07:30 → 08:40.

Getting back. CAM line 113 (new no. 702), Baía d'Abra → Funchal, last bus: Monday to Friday 19:35 → 21:05; Saturdays 19:35 → 21:05; Sundays and holidays 18:15 → 19:45.

## PR11 Vereda dos Balcões …

Getting there. Ribeiro Frio, where the walk starts and ends, is a bus stop. CAM's Santana-line buses, Funchal → Ribeiro Frio, first bus: Monday to Friday 08:10 → 08:50; Saturdays 07:30 → 08:12; Sundays and holidays 07:30 → 08:12.

Getting back. CAM's Santana-line buses, Ribeiro Frio → Funchal, last bus: Monday to Friday 18:12 → 19:00; Saturdays, Sundays and holidays 18:30 → 19:20.

## PR19 Caminho Real do Paul do Mar …

Getting there. Prazeres, where the walk starts, is a bus stop. Rodoeste line 142, Funchal → Prazeres, bus: every day 08:05 → 11:15.

Getting back. The walk ends at Paul do Mar, which has a bus back to Funchal. Rodoeste line 142, Paul do Mar → Funchal, bus: Monday to Friday 14:15 → 16:55. Rodoeste line 80, Paul do Mar → Funchal, bus: Saturdays, Sundays and holidays 17:00 → 18:40. On weekdays that leaves about 3 hours between arriving at Prazeres and the bus back.

## PR20 Vereda do Jardim do Mar …

Getting there. Prazeres, where the walk starts, is a bus stop. Rodoeste line 142, Funchal → Prazeres, bus: every day 08:05 → 11:15.

Getting back. The walk ends at Jardim do Mar, which has a bus back to Funchal. Rodoeste line 142, Jardim do Mar → Funchal, bus: Monday to Friday 14:20 → 16:55. Rodoeste line 80, Jardim do Mar → Funchal, bus: Saturdays, Sundays and holidays 17:05 → 18:40. On weekdays that leaves about 3 hours between arriving at Prazeres and the bus back.

## Bus plus a taxi

## PR9 Levada do Caldeirão Verde …

Getting there. No bus goes up to Queimadas. Take a CAM bus to Santana, then a taxi up to the Queimadas forest park (ask the fare when you book). CAM's Santana-line buses, Funchal → Santana, first bus: Monday to Friday 07:30 → 09:00; Saturdays 07:30 → 09:13; Sundays and holidays 07:30 → 09:18.

Getting back. CAM's Santana-line buses, Santana → Funchal, last bus: Monday to Friday 17:25 → 19:00; Saturdays 17:28 → 19:20; Sundays and holidays 17:28 → 19:20.

## PR9.1 Levada do Caldeirão Verde - um caminho para todos …

Getting there. No bus goes up to Queimadas. Take a CAM bus to Santana, then a taxi up to the Queimadas forest park (ask the fare when you book). CAM's Santana-line buses, Funchal → Santana, first bus: Monday to Friday 07:30 → 09:00; Saturdays 07:30 → 09:13; Sundays and holidays 07:30 → 09:18.

Getting back. CAM's Santana-line buses, Santana → Funchal, last bus: Monday to Friday 17:25 → 19:00; Saturdays 17:28 → 19:20; Sundays and holidays 17:28 → 19:20.

## Bus at one end only

## PR2 Vereda do Urzal …

Getting there. Curral das Freiras, where the walk starts, is a bus stop. Horários do Funchal line 81 (new no. 181), Funchal → Curral das Freiras, first bus: Monday to Friday 06:55; Saturdays 07:40; Sundays and holidays 06:40.

Getting back. We found no bus from Lombo do Urzal, where the walk ends: book a taxi or arrange a pick-up before you set off.

## PR10 Levada do Furado …

Getting there. Ribeiro Frio, where the walk starts, is a bus stop. CAM's Santana-line buses, Funchal → Ribeiro Frio, first bus: Monday to Friday 08:10 → 08:50; Saturdays 07:30 → 08:12; Sundays and holidays 07:30 → 08:12.

Getting back. Lines 53 and 78 (new no. 825) run via Portela, but their timetables print no time at Portela: ask CAM for the time it passes, or take a taxi.

## PR3.1 Caminho Real do Monte …

Getting there. We found no bus to Ribeira das Cales, where the walk starts: you need a car, a taxi or a transfer.

Getting back. The walk ends at Monte, which has a bus back to Funchal. Horários do Funchal line 21, Monte → Funchal, last bus: Monday to Friday 19:05; Saturdays 18:05; Sundays and holidays 18:05.

## PR1.3 Vereda da Encumeada …

Getting there. The walk starts at the Pico Ruivo shelter, which no bus or road reaches: you get there on foot by PR1 or PR1.2.

Getting back. The walk ends at Encumeada, which has a bus back to Funchal. Rodoeste line 6, Encumeada → Funchal, bus: every day 16:00 → 17:05. It is the only bus of the day from there, so don't miss it.

## PR17 Caminho do Pináculo e Folhadal …

Getting there. We found no bus to Lombo do Mouro, where the walk starts: you need a car, a taxi or a transfer.

Getting back. The walk ends at Encumeada, which has a bus back to Funchal. Rodoeste line 6, Encumeada → Funchal, bus: every day 16:00 → 17:05. It is the only bus of the day from there, so don't miss it.

## PR5 Vereda das Funduras …

Getting there. Lines 53 and 78 (new no. 825) run via Portela, but their timetables print no time at Portela: ask CAM for the time it passes, or take a taxi.

Getting back. The walk ends at Maroços, which has a bus back to Funchal. CAM line 156 (new no. 704), Maroços → Funchal, last bus: Monday to Friday 21:10 → 22:20; Saturdays 22:35 → 23:45; Sundays and holidays 22:35 → 23:45.

## No bus: Rabaçal, Paul da Serra, Fanal

None of the bus lines published on SIGA serves these trailheads. You need a car, a taxi or a tour transfer.

- PR6 Levada das 25 Fontes … · start: Rabaçal

- PR6.1 Levada do Risco … · start: Rabaçal

- PR6.2 Levada do Alecrim … · start: Rabaçal

- PR6.3 Vereda da Lagoa do Vento … · start: Rabaçal

- PR6.4 Levada Velha do Rabaçal … · start: Rabaçal

- PR6.8 Levada do Paul II - Um caminho para todos … · start: Rabaçal

- PR6.5 Vereda do Pico Fernandes … · start: Paul da Serra

- PR6.6 Vereda do Túnel do Cavalo … · start: Paul da Serra

- PR13.1 Vereda da Palha Carga … · start: Paul da Serra

- PR27 Glaciar de Planalto … · start: Paul da Serra

- PR13 Vereda do Fanal … · start: Fanal

- PR28 Levada da Rocha Vermelha … · start: Fanal

## Questions

## Which levada walks can I do by bus from Funchal?

Four trails have a public bus to the start and back from the end: PR8 São Lourenço (CAM line 113 to Baía d'Abra), PR11 Balcões (CAM's Santana buses to Ribeiro Frio), and PR19 and PR20 (Rodoeste line 142 to Prazeres in the morning, back from Paul do Mar or Jardim do Mar in the afternoon). Six more have a bus at one end only.

## Is there a bus to 25 Fontes and Rabaçal?

No. None of the bus lines published on SIGA serves Rabaçal, the Paul da Serra plateau or the Fanal, so PR6 25 Fontes, PR6.1 Risco, PR13 Fanal and the other trails up there need a car, a taxi or a transfer.

## Is there a bus to São Lourenço?

Yes. CAM line 113 (new no. 702) runs every day from Funchal to Baía d'Abra, where PR8 starts and ends. The first bus leaves Funchal at 07:30.

## Can I get to Caldeirão Verde by bus?

Partly. CAM buses run from Funchal to Santana, but none goes up to the Queimadas forest park where PR9 starts: take a taxi from Santana for the last stretch.

## Where can I find the bus timetables?

On SIGA (siga.madeira.gov.pt/horarios), the Region's public transport site, which publishes the operators' timetables. Check them before you travel: times can change.

- Best levada walks in Madeira

## Sources

Bus times: the operators' timetables (CAM, Rodoeste, Horários do Funchal) published on SIGA, checked 3 Oct 2026. Times at intermediate stops are approximate; no buses on 25 December; check before you travel. Trail status: IFCN trail warnings.

best.text:
## The best levada walks in Madeira, and which are open today

We compared nine of the best-known “best levadas” lists and kept the trails most of them agree on. Each one comes with its live official status, the 2026 fee and the warnings on IFCN's trailhead panel.

The short answer: the levadas that most guides rank highest are PR9 Caldeirão Verde (8 of 9 lists), PR7 Levada do Moinho (7), PR6 25 Fontes and PR18 Levada do Rei (6 each), then PR11 Balcões, PR14 Levada dos Cedros, PR16 Fajã do Rodrigues and PR17 Pináculo e Folhadal. All are booking-only on SIMplifica at €4.50 per person in 2026. Not all of them are open: PR7 was on IFCN's closed list when we wrote this, so check the badge next to each trail before you plan the day.

Each trail below shows its status from the official IFCN list, with IFCN's own “updated” date.

## The list, ranked by how many guides pick it

Why go comes from each trail's official Visit Madeira page; Watch out comes from IFCN's trailhead panel. Hover over or tap a badge to read the official IFCN note.

## 1. Levada do Caldeirão Verde PR9…

8.7 km (17.4 km round trip) · 6:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 8 of 9 guides

Why go: A laurel-forest levada “punctuated by escarpments and mountains”, through four tunnels carved in the rock, to the Caldeirão Verde waterfall basin.

Watch out: Four tunnels: carry a torch. IFCN's panel also warns of vertigo and a slippery path.

Tunnels: bring a torchIFCN vertigo warning

## 2. Levada do Moinho PR7…

10.5 km · 3:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 7 of 9 guides

Why go: A 10.5 km levada named after the water mills it once fed, almost entirely through laurel forest.

Watch out: IFCN had it on its closed list at the time of writing: check the badge. The long tunnel people mention is on the unofficial Levada Nova extension, not on PR7.

Slippery in parts

## 3. Levada das 25 Fontes PR6…

4.3 km (8.6 km round trip) · 3 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 6 of 9 guides

Why go: The lagoon fed by 25 springs from Paul da Serra, with views over the Ribeira da Janela valley.

Watch out: IFCN: “PR 6 can cause vertigo”; don't lean on the barriers. Part of the route is one-way, so follow the loop.

IFCN vertigo warning

## 4. Levada do Rei PR18…

5.3 km (10.6 km round trip) · 3:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 6 of 9 guides

Why go: It ends at Ribeiro Bonito, “an isolated natural sanctuary” of laurel forest, and passes the São Jorge water mill, still working.

Watch out: Most guides call it easy, but IFCN's panel warns of vertigo and a slippery path in places. One very short tunnel; a guide says no torch is needed.

IFCN vertigo warningShort tunnel, no torch needed

## 5. Vereda dos Balcões PR11…

1.5 km (3 km round trip) · 1:30 h · Easy · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 5 of 9 guides

Why go: Short and easy, 1.5 km each way, to the Balcões viewpoint over the laurel-forest valleys and the central peaks.

Watch out: No vertigo warning on the IFCN panel. The viewpoint itself looks over big drops, but it's fenced. Weather changes fast; the path can be slippery.

Low exposure

## 6. Levada dos Cedros PR14…

7.2 km · 3 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 4 of 9 guides

Why go: Centuries-old til trees in the Fanal forest, along one of the oldest levadas, dug in the 17th century.

Watch out: IFCN's panel warns of vertigo and a slippery path.

IFCN vertigo warningSlippery in parts

## 7. Levada Fajã do Rodrigues PR16…

3.9 km (7.8 km round trip) · 3:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 4 of 9 guides

Why go: “Tunnels are common” on this one, with waterfalls and views over the São Vicente valley.

Watch out: IFCN warns of vertigo and says to carry a torch. The last tunnel is about 1 km long (20–25 minutes).

Tunnels: bring a torchIFCN vertigo warning

## 8. Caminho do Pináculo e Folhadal PR17…

15 km · 6:30 h · Difficult · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 4 of 9 guides

Why go: The Pináculo viewpoint over the Ribeira Brava valley, then a Levada do Norte section with tunnels and waterfalls.

Watch out: A long route: IFCN asks for physical preparation, warm waterproof layers and a torch for the tunnels. Guides rate it high exposure. When we wrote this only part of it was open: check the badge.

Tunnels: bring a torchHigh exposure (guides)Long day

## 9. Levada do Furado PR10…

11 km · 5 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 3 of 9 guides

Why go: One of the oldest public levadas, with views of Faial, Porto da Cruz and Penha d'Águia.

Watch out: IFCN's panel warns of vertigo and says there are tunnels, so carry a torch. IFCN's notices have also mentioned a rockfall closure between Ribeiro Frio and Lamaceiros: read the official note before you go.

Tunnels: bring a torchIFCN vertigo warning

## 10. Vereda do Fanal PR13…

10.8 km · 4 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 3 of 9 guides

Why go: The old til forest on the Paul da Serra plateau. A path (vereda) rather than a levada, but on many “best” lists.

Watch out: IFCN warns of frequent fog and the risk of getting lost: stay on the trail and bring warm clothes.

Fog: stay on the trailLow exposure

## 11. Vereda da Ponta de São Lourenço PR8…

4 km · 2:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50 · Picked by 3 of 9 guides

Why go: A semi-arid peninsula with seabird colonies and, with luck, monk seals. A path rather than a levada.

Watch out: IFCN: keep away from the cliff edge, the ground is unstable in many places; carry water. Works with signposted detours from 30 September 2026 for at least 270 days.

Cliff edges

## Booking and fees for all of them

Every trail here needs a SIMplifica booking for a time slot: €4.50 per person per trail in 2026, or €3 through an operator with an IFCN protocol. Children aged 12 and under don't pay but must be on the booking. Doing two or more in one day? The day pass is €9 (PR1 is never included).

## Popular, but not official PR trails

Levada Nova, Rocha Vermelha via the Calheta council tunnel, Levada dos Tornos, Caldeirão do Inferno beyond PR9 and the Rota da Banana also appear on some lists. They aren't official PR routes, so they're not on SIMplifica and IFCN doesn't maintain or recommend them.

## Questions

## Which is the best levada walk in Madeira?

Levada do Caldeirão Verde (PR9) is the one most guides put first: 8 of the 9 lists we compared include it. Next come Levada do Moinho (PR7), 25 Fontes (PR6) and Levada do Rei (PR18). Check the live status first: PR7 was on IFCN's closed list at the time of writing.

## How much does a levada walk cost in 2026?

Official PR trails cost €4.50 per person (PR1 costs €10.50), booked online on SIMplifica for a time slot. Children aged 12 and under are exempt but must be on the booking. Through an operator with an IFCN protocol the fee is €3.

## Which of the best levadas have tunnels?

Caldeirão Verde (PR9, four tunnels), Fajã do Rodrigues (PR16, the last tunnel about 1 km), Pináculo e Folhadal (PR17) and Levada do Furado (PR10). IFCN's trailhead panels say to carry a torch on all four.

## Next steps

- Easiest levadas without vertigo: an honest ranking by exposure.

- Which levadas need a torch?: every tunnel trail in one table.

- Every trail, open or closed: the live board for all trails.

- 2026 trail fees: passes, exemptions and operator rates.

Sources: consensus from nine ranking pages compared on 30 Sep 2026 (TheRoadReel, MadeiraLovers, JourneyEra, Much Better Adventures, schmale-pfade.de, 22places, madera.org.pl, vagamundos.pt, Visit Madeira blog); “Why go” lines from each trail's official Visit Madeira page; warnings from IFCN's trailhead panels; status from the official IFCN warnings list; fees from Portaria 48/2026 (Anexo I).

easy.text:
## Easiest levada walks without vertigo

Ranked by the official warnings on IFCN's trailhead panels and checked against independent guides. If we found no sourced rating for a trail, it isn't listed.

The short answer: for the least exposure, choose the two purpose-built accessible routes, PR6.8 Levada do Paul II and PR9.1 Caldeirão Verde “um caminho para todos”, or PR11 Vereda dos Balcões, PR13 Fanal and PR6.2 Levada do Alecrim. Be careful with the usual “easy” tips: IFCN's own trailhead panels warn of danger of vertigo on PR18 Levada do Rei and PR14 Levada dos Cedros, even though most guides call them easy. If drops bother you, skip PR1, PR6 25 Fontes, PR8, PR9, PR16, PR17 and PR19. All need a SIMplifica booking; the fee is €4.50 (PR1 €10.50).

Each trail below shows its status from the official IFCN list, with IFCN's own “updated” date.

## How we rate exposure

Low: built for accessibility, or no vertigo warning on the IFCN panel plus at least two independent guides calling it easy. Moderate: an official warning that guides play down. High: an official vertigo or cliff warning that guides agree with, or two or more guides rating it high. Trails with no sourced rating are left out.

## 1. Lowest exposure: start here

## 1. Levada do Paul II - Um caminho para todos PR6.8…

1.2 km · 30 min · Fee €4.50

Built as “a path for everyone”, including people with reduced mobility (Visit Madeira). A short walk; IFCN's panel only warns about changing weather.

Accessible routeLow exposure

## 2. Levada do Caldeirão Verde - um caminho para todos PR9.1…

1.9 km · 45 min · Fee €4.50

Designed for people with motor and visual disabilities: about 2 km in 45 minutes (Visit Madeira).

Accessible routeLow exposure

## 3. Vereda dos Balcões PR11…

1.5 km (3 km round trip) · 1:30 h · Easy · Fee €4.50

Visit Madeira calls it easy, IFCN's panel has no vertigo warning, and guides describe a “wide, level path” (juliedawnfox). One caveat: the Balcões viewpoint at the end looks over big drops, though it's fenced (hikingmadeira).

Low exposure

## 4. Vereda do Fanal PR13…

10.8 km · 4 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50

No vertigo warning on IFCN's panel; its warning is fog, which makes it easy to lose your way. Guides rate it among the gentlest (madeirahiking.org, madeiralovers). It's long, but you can turn back whenever you like.

Low exposureFog: stay on the trail

## 5. Levada do Alecrim PR6.2…

3.5 km (7 km round trip) · 2:30 h · Easy · Fee €4.50

Two independent guides say it has no serious exposure (hikingmadeira; waldspaziergang.org, as the “Rosmarin-Levada”). There's no IFCN panel for it. The “tunnels” Visit Madeira mentions are arches of heather, not rock tunnels.

Low exposure

## 2. Called easy, but with an official warning

These often appear on “no vertigo” lists. They're mostly gentle, but IFCN's panels disagree with that label in places, so go knowing that.

## Levada do Rei PR18…

5.3 km (10.6 km round trip) · 3:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50

Most guides call it one of the easiest levadas: “no steep drop-offs… no narrow ledges” (hikingmadeira). IFCN's own trailhead panel still says: danger of vertigo, path may be slippery. Our reading: mostly wide and gentle, but not free of drops everywhere.

IFCN vertigo warningShort tunnel, no torch needed

## Levada dos Cedros PR14…

7.2 km · 3 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50

madeirahiking.org rates it “very low exposure” and madeiralovers calls it easy. But IFCN's panel says danger of vertigo, and Visit Madeira describes passing “the steep slope of the right bank of the Ribeira da Janela”.

IFCN vertigo warningSlippery in parts

## Levada do Furado PR10…

11 km · 5 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50

madeirahiking.org puts it in its low-exposure group but mentions “some narrow levada sections with drops”. IFCN's panel says danger of vertigo, and that there are tunnels, so carry a torch.

IFCN vertigo warningTunnels: bring a torch

## Levada da Rocha Vermelha PR28…

10.8 km · 4 h · Fee €4.50

IFCN's panel warns of “technical and physical particularities”: make sure it suits you. The famous long tunnel is on Calheta council's access route from Malhada, which the council describes as exposed, without protective walls and liable to cause vertigo.

Tunnels: bring a torch

## 3. Trails with drops: skip these if you have vertigo

- PR1 Vereda do Areeiro …
6.1 km · 3 h · Moderate · Fee €10.50
Narrow ridge, steep slopes and a carved rock staircase around Pico das Torres; named vertigo-prone by hikingmadeira and madeirahiking.org.

- PR6 Levada das 25 Fontes …
4.3 km (8.6 km round trip) · 3 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50
IFCN's panel: “PR 6 can cause vertigo”. Guides mention narrow ledges and “hair raising drops”.

- PR8 Vereda da Ponta de São Lourenço …
4 km · 2:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50
IFCN's panel: don't go near the cliff face, the ground is unstable in many places. “Many unprotected edges” (hikingmadeira).

- PR9 Levada do Caldeirão Verde …
8.7 km (17.4 km round trip) · 6:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50
IFCN's panel: danger of vertigo. Guides mention narrow ledges and dark tunnels.

- PR16 Levada Fajã do Rodrigues …
3.9 km (7.8 km round trip) · 3:30 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50
IFCN's panel: danger of vertigo. A narrow levada path with drops, plus long tunnels.

- PR17 Caminho do Pináculo e Folhadal …
15 km · 6:30 h · Difficult · Fee €4.50
No vertigo line on the IFCN panel, but guides say “not for vertigo sufferers” (madeirahiking.org) and “not for the faint-hearted” (Visit Madeira blog).

- PR19 Caminho Real do Paul do Mar …
1.8 km · 1:20 h · Moderate · Fee €4.50
IFCN's panel: danger of vertigo, its only warning.

## Not rated here

Visit Madeira calls PR6.1 Levada do Risco and PR6.3 Lagoa do Vento easy, but we found no sourced exposure rating, so they aren't ranked. Levada da Serra do Faial and Levada do Castelejo appear on some “no vertigo” lists, but they aren't official PR trails, so IFCN doesn't maintain them.

Worried about tunnels rather than heights? On PR16 the tunnels are low enough that you have to stoop (sayyestomadeira). See which levadas need a torch.

On the trails board, the No vertigo filter shows which low-exposure trails are open right now.

## Questions

## Which levada is easiest if I'm afraid of heights?

The accessible routes PR6.8 Levada do Paul II and PR9.1 Caldeirão Verde “um caminho para todos” are built for everyone. Of the regular trails, PR11 Vereda dos Balcões, PR13 Fanal and PR6.2 Levada do Alecrim have the least exposure, with no vertigo warning on IFCN's panels. The Balcões viewpoint itself looks over big drops, but it is fenced.

## Is Levada do Rei OK if I get vertigo?

Most guides call Levada do Rei (PR18) one of the easiest levadas, with wide paths. But IFCN's official trailhead panel warns of danger of vertigo and a slippery path, so expect some exposed spots. The same goes for Levada dos Cedros (PR14).

## Which levadas should I avoid if I have vertigo?

PR1 Pico do Areeiro to Pico Ruivo, PR6 25 Fontes, PR8 Ponta de São Lourenço, PR9 Caldeirão Verde, PR16 Fajã do Rodrigues, PR17 Pináculo e Folhadal and PR19 Caminho Real do Paul do Mar. Each has an official vertigo or cliff warning or is rated high exposure by guides.

## Next steps

- The best levada walks: with live status for each.

- Which levadas need a torch?: every tunnel trail in one table.

- Every trail, open or closed: the live board for all trails.

- 2026 trail fees: passes, exemptions and operator rates.

Sources: exposure warnings from IFCN's IFCN trailhead panels (read 30 Sep 2026); descriptions from each trail's official Visit Madeira page; guides: hikingmadeira, juliedawnfox, madeirahiking.org, madeiralovers, waldspaziergang.org, sayyestomadeira, CM Calheta; status from the official IFCN warnings list.

## Which levadas need a torch or headlamp?

Every official PR trail with tunnels, from IFCN's trailhead panels and Visit Madeira, with the live status of each.

The short answer: bring a torch or headlamp on PR16 Fajã do Rodrigues (the last tunnel is about 1 km, 20–25 minutes), PR9 Caldeirão Verde (four tunnels), PR6.6 Túnel do Cavalo (about 800 m), PR17 Pináculo e Folhadal, PR10 Levada do Furado, PR28 Rocha Vermelha, PR6.4 Levada Velha do Rabaçal and PR1 Areeiro–Ruivo: IFCN tells you to on each one. PR18 Levada do Rei has only a very short tunnel, and the standard PR6 25 Fontes route has none.

Each trail below shows its status from the official IFCN list, with IFCN's own “updated” date.

## Every PR trail with tunnels

Official PR trails with tunnels. “Torch?” is what IFCN's trailhead panel (or PR1 leaflet) says.

On the trails board, the Has tunnels filter shows which tunnel trails are open right now.

## What to bring

- A headlamp rather than your phone. It keeps both hands free on a wet, uneven floor, and your phone battery stays for maps and emergencies (112). IFCN's panels simply say “carry a torch”.

- One light per person, plus spare batteries or a charged power bank. PR16's last tunnel alone takes 20–25 minutes.

- A rain jacket. Tunnels can drip: guides describe the Túnel do Cavalo as long, wet and unlit.

- Shoes with grip. IFCN warns that paths on these trails can be slippery.

- Tall? Expect to stoop in low sections (reported on PR16).

## Tunnels people mention that aren't on the PR route

- The “800 m tunnel” at 25 Fontes is the Túnel do Cavalo on PR6.6, its own trail. The standard PR6 route (Rabaçal to 25 Fontes, back by the Bypass) has no tunnel.

- The 1.6–1.8 km “Rocha Vermelha tunnel” is on Calheta council's access route from Malhada (about 1.7 km, says the council), not on official PR28, which starts at Fanal.

- The long tunnel on “Levada do Moinho” walks is on the unofficial Levada Nova extension. Official PR7 shows no tunnel on its IFCN panel or its Visit Madeira page.

- The “heather tunnels” on PR6.2 and the plant “tunnels” on PR18 are arches of vegetation, not rock tunnels.

- On Porto Santo, PR3 Levada do Pico do Castelo has a tunnel with a slippery floor; IFCN says to bring a flashlight.

## Questions

## Which levadas need a torch?

IFCN's trailhead panels say to carry a torch on PR9 Caldeirão Verde, PR16 Fajã do Rodrigues, PR17 Pináculo e Folhadal, PR10 Levada do Furado, PR6.6 Túnel do Cavalo, PR6.4 Levada Velha do Rabaçal and PR28 Rocha Vermelha. IFCN's PR1 leaflet says the same for Pico do Areeiro to Pico Ruivo.

## Is a phone light enough in the tunnels?

IFCN doesn't say; its panels just say to carry a torch. A headlamp is the practical choice: your hands stay free on a wet, uneven floor and your phone battery stays for navigation and emergencies. PR16's last tunnel takes 20–25 minutes to walk.

## Does Levada das 25 Fontes have a tunnel?

Not on the standard PR6 route from Rabaçal. The 800 m tunnel people mention is the Túnel do Cavalo, on the separate trail PR6.6. You need a torch for that one.
